intro.en: Widely regarded as one of the first generation of modern Chinese architects, and among the earliest women in the field. She joined survey, preservation, teaching, design and writing into one practice: she helped found architecture programmes at two universities, measured ancient buildings as a core member of the Society for Research in Chinese Architecture, and worked on the national emblem and the Monument to the People's Heroes.
intro.zh: 被广泛视为中国现代第一代、也是最早的女性建筑师之一。她把建筑调查、保护、教学、设计与写作连在一起：参与创建两所大学的建筑教育，作为中国营造学社核心成员测绘古建筑，并参与国徽与人民英雄纪念碑设计。

timeline.en: Penn's architecture school did not grant degrees to women, so she enrolled in fine arts — and completed nearly all the architecture coursework anyway, serving as a teaching assistant in architectural design. Her transcript shows top marks in course after course.
timeline.zh: 宾大建筑系当时不向女性授予学位，她注册美术专业，却完成了绝大多数建筑学课程并担任建筑设计课助教；成绩单上多门课获最高等级。

coda.en: On 18 May 2024 Penn's Weitzman School formally awarded her a posthumous Bachelor of Architecture at commencement — a century late.
coda.zh: 2024 年 5 月 18 日，宾大韦茨曼设计学院在毕业典礼上正式向她追授建筑学学士学位，迟到一百年。

timeline.en: With Liang Sicheng and others she helped found the architecture department at Northeastern University — among the first in China — and in 1946 helped found Tsinghua's. She also designed Northeastern's emblem.
timeline.zh: 与梁思成等人参与创建东北大学建筑系——中国最早的建筑学系之一；1946 年又参与创建清华大学建筑系。她还设计了东北大学「白山黑水」校徽。

timeline.en: As a core member of the Society for Research in Chinese Architecture, she surveyed and measured ancient buildings across Hebei, Shanxi and other provinces, and helped organise the photographs, drawings and reports. The thousands of sites recorded were the team's collective achievement — not hers and Liang Sicheng's alone.
timeline.zh: 作为中国营造学社核心成员，赴河北、山西等多省调查、测绘古建筑，并参与整理照片、图纸与研究报告。数千处遗存的总量属于营造学社团队成果，不应全部归到她与梁思成两人名下。

timeline.en: Wrote the introduction to Liang Sicheng's Qing Structural Regulations — one of the founding texts of modern Chinese architectural theory. Her work was never only measuring and drafting; it was the theoretical frame.
timeline.zh: 为梁思成《清式营造则例》撰写绪论——中国建筑理论现代化的起点文本之一。她做的不只是测绘制图，还有理论框架。

timeline.en: Edited and introduced an anthology of fiction for Ta Kung Pao's literary supplement. The salon she hosted was one of the most important intellectual rooms in 1930s Beiping; writers such as Xiao Qian were launched from it.
timeline.zh: 主编《大公报文艺丛刊小说选》并撰序；她主持的沙龙是三十年代北平最重要的知识现场之一，萧乾等人从这里被推出来。

timeline.en: Identified the donor inscription naming "the female disciple Ning Gongyu" on a beam of Foguang Temple's East Hall; the team cross-checked it against the dated sutra pillar outside, confirming the hall was built in 857 — a landmark discovery in Chinese architectural history.
timeline.zh: 在佛光寺东大殿梁架上辨认出「女弟子宁公遇」题记；营造学社团队再与殿前经幢纪年互证，确认大殿建于唐大中十一年（857），成为中国古建筑史的标志性发现。

timeline.en: With Liang Sicheng she organised a design group from Tsinghua's architecture faculty that produced the accepted scheme for the national emblem of the People's Republic of China; Gao Zhuang then revised and finalised the model.
timeline.zh: 与梁思成组织清华营建系教师组成设计组，参与完成中华人民共和国国徽方案；高庄随后负责国徽模型的修改与定型。

timeline.en: Designed the wreath reliefs on the base of the Monument to the People's Heroes; rescued the dying cloisonné craft and designed the cloisonné state gifts for the Asia-Pacific Peace Conference.
timeline.zh: 设计人民英雄纪念碑基座的花圈浮雕；抢救濒临失传的景泰蓝工艺，并设计了亚太和平会议的景泰蓝国礼。

timeline.en: Argued publicly for preserving old Beijing, backing the Liang–Chen proposal to move the administrative centre west and urging that the city walls be turned into an encircling park. The plan was rejected.
timeline.zh: 积极参与北京古城保护论争，支持梁思成与陈占祥提出的行政中心西移方案，并主张把城墙转化为环城公园。方案未被采纳。

timeline.en: Full professor in Tsinghua's architecture department, teaching Chinese architectural history; from her sickbed she kept revising A History of Chinese Architecture and co-wrote Historical Stages in the Development of Chinese Architecture with Liang Sicheng and Mo Zongjiang.
timeline.zh: 任清华大学建筑系一级教授，讲授中国建筑史；在病中继续协助《中国建筑史》的修改，并与梁思成、莫宗江合著《中国建筑发展的历史阶段》。

story.en:
She climbed the rafters of thousand-year-old temples with notebooks and measuring tape, documenting China's ancient architecture before war could erase it — often while coughing blood from tuberculosis.

She co-designed the national emblem of modern China. She wrote poetry that is still recited. She did all of it while critics discussed her beauty instead of her blueprints.

Let them talk about your face while you build what outlasts them all.
story.zh:
她爬上千年古寺的房梁，用皮尺和笔记本为中国古建筑留下测稿，赶在战火抹去它们之前——常常一边咳血，一边工作。

她参与设计了新中国的国徽。她写下至今仍被传诵的诗。而做这一切时，评论家们谈论的是她的容貌，而不是她的图纸。

让他们去议论你的脸吧——你只管建造那些比他们活得更久的东西。

intro.en: She wrote gender equality into American constitutional law one case at a time: first dismantling statutes that treated men and women differently through litigation design, then shaping equal-protection doctrine as a judge and justice. Law firms turned her down when she was job-hunting; she went on to rewrite the legal environment those firms worked in.
intro.zh: 她把性别平等一步步写进美国宪法判例：先以诉讼设计拆除区别对待男女的法律，再以法官和大法官身份塑造平等保护原则。求职时多家律所拒绝过她；后来她改写了这些机构所处的法律环境。

timeline.en: One of nine women in a Harvard Law class of five hundred. At a dinner the dean asked them to justify taking a man's place.
timeline.zh: 哈佛法学院五百人的年级里九名女生之一。院长在晚宴上要她们说明凭什么占了一个男人的位置。

timeline.en: Graduated tied for first at Columbia Law and was still turned down by New York firms; she took a federal district court clerkship instead.
timeline.zh: 以并列第一从哥伦比亚法学院毕业，却仍被多家纽约律所拒绝；随后获得联邦地区法院法官助理职位。

timeline.en: Joined the Rutgers law faculty, one of fewer than twenty women teaching law in the country — and hid her pregnancy for its full term to keep the job.
timeline.zh: 进入罗格斯法学院任教，成为当时全美不到二十名女性法学教授之一——为保住教职，她整个孕期都在藏。

timeline.en: Helped launch the Women's Rights Law Reporter with students, lawyers and activists, serving as its founding faculty adviser; it was the first US journal devoted to women's rights law.
timeline.zh: 与学生、法律工作者和女权活动者共同推动 Women's Rights Law Reporter 创刊，并担任创刊教师顾问；它是美国最早专门研究女性权利法律的期刊。

timeline.en: Wrote the ACLU's brief in Reed v. Reed without arguing it, and put Pauli Murray and Dorothy Kenyon on the cover to credit their theoretical work. The Supreme Court struck down a sex-based classification under the Equal Protection Clause for the first time.
timeline.zh: 为 ACLU 撰写 Reed v. Reed 诉状（未出庭），并以署名致敬 Pauli Murray 与 Dorothy Kenyon 的理论工作；最高法院首次以平等保护条款推翻性别分类法律。

timeline.en: Moritz v. Commissioner: won a caregiver's tax deduction for a man. The case let her show that sex stereotyping harms men and women alike, and became the key test of her later litigation strategy.
timeline.zh: Moritz v. Commissioner：为一位男性照护者争取税收减免并胜诉。这一案件帮助她证明性别定型同时伤害男性与女性，并成为后续诉讼策略的关键试验。

timeline.en: Co-founded the ACLU Women's Rights Project, building a systematic litigation strategy against sex discrimination; the same year she became Columbia Law's first tenured woman professor.
timeline.zh: 共同创办 ACLU 女性权利项目，搭建起对抗性别歧视的系统诉讼战略；同年成为哥伦比亚法学院第一位女性终身教授。

timeline.en: Argued six sex-discrimination cases before the Supreme Court and won five — sometimes for male plaintiffs, to show that inequality costs everyone.
timeline.zh: 在最高法院辩护六起性别歧视案，赢下五起——有时是为男性辩护，以证明不平等对谁都有代价。

timeline.en: Thirteen years as a judge on the D.C. Circuit. This is where she learned to write opinions and to work alongside conservative colleagues.
timeline.zh: 任哥伦比亚特区联邦上诉法院法官十三年。她在这里学会了怎么写判决、怎么和保守派同僚共事。

timeline.en: Appointed to the US Supreme Court — the second woman in its 204-year history.
timeline.zh: 出任美国最高法院大法官——该院 204 年历史上的第二位女性。

timeline.en: Wrote the majority opinion in United States v. Virginia, ending male-only admission at the Virginia Military Institute.
timeline.zh: 撰写 United States v. Virginia 多数意见，终结弗吉尼亚军事学院的男性专属招生。

timeline.en: Read her dissent from the bench in Ledbetter v. Goodyear, directly prompting the Lilly Ledbetter Fair Pay Act of 2009 — a lost case that changed the law.
timeline.zh: 在 Ledbetter v. Goodyear 案中当庭宣读异议意见，直接催生 2009 年 Lilly Ledbetter 公平薪酬法案——一场输掉的官司改掉了法律。

timeline.en: Wrote the Shelby County dissent ("throwing away your umbrella in a rainstorm because you are not getting wet"); the same year she became the first Supreme Court justice to officiate a same-sex wedding.
timeline.zh: 写下 Shelby County 案异议（「在暴雨中扔掉伞，因为你没淋湿」）；同年成为第一位主持同性婚礼的最高法院大法官。

story.en:
Nine law firms refused to hire her — top of her class at Columbia, but a woman, a mother, a Jew.

So she changed the law itself. Case by careful case, she dismantled gender discrimination — sometimes arguing for men, to show the court that inequality cuts everyone.

"Fight for the things that you care about, but do it in a way that will lead others to join you."
story.zh:
九家律所拒绝雇用她——哥伦比亚法学院的第一名，但她是女人、是母亲、是犹太人。

于是她去改变法律本身。一案接一案，她拆解了性别歧视的法条——有时为男性辩护，让法庭看到不平等伤害所有人。

「为你在乎的事而战，但要用让他人愿意与你同行的方式。」

intro.en: The first woman to win a Nobel Prize, the first person to win two, and still the only person to win in two different natural sciences. She did more than discover elements: she built research institutions, and organised X-ray technology into frontline medicine in the First World War.
intro.zh: 她是第一位获得诺贝尔奖的女性，也是第一位两度获诺奖的人；至今仍是唯一分别在物理学与化学两个自然科学门类获奖的人。她不只发现元素，还建立研究机构，并把 X 光技术组织进第一次世界大战的前线医疗。

timeline.en: Left Poland, where universities did not admit women, for the Sorbonne. Lived in a garret on bread, butter and tea.
timeline.zh: 离开不招女生的波兰前往索邦，靠面包、黄油和茶住在阁楼里。

timeline.en: Discovered two new elements — polonium, named for her homeland, and radium — and coined the word "radioactivity," arguing it was a property of the atom itself rather than a chemical reaction. That insight went deeper than the elements.
timeline.zh: 发现两种新元素：钋（以祖国命名）与镭；并提出「放射性」一词，指出放射性是原子本身的属性而非化学反应——这比发现元素更根本。

timeline.en: Won the Nobel Prize in Physics, the first woman ever to do so; the same year she became the first woman in France to earn a doctorate in physics.
timeline.zh: 获诺贝尔物理学奖，史上第一位女性得主；同年成为法国第一位取得物理学博士学位的女性。

timeline.en: Became the first woman professor in the Sorbonne's 650-year history.
timeline.zh: 成为索邦六百五十年历史上第一位女教授。

timeline.en: With André-Louis Debierne, isolated metallic radium by electrolysis, then helped establish the international radium standard. The Curies never patented their separation method, leaving it free for other laboratories to use.
timeline.zh: 与 André-Louis Debierne 以电解法制得金属镭；随后参与确立国际镭标准。居里夫妇没有为镭的分离方法申请专利，使其他实验室能够使用这套方法。

timeline.en: Won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry. She remains the only person to have won in two different sciences.
timeline.zh: 获诺贝尔化学奖。她至今仍是唯一在两个不同科学领域获诺奖的人。

timeline.en: The Radium Institute in Paris was founded jointly by the University of Paris and the Pasteur Institute, with her leading the physics and chemistry laboratory; she went on raising funds until the Radium Institute in Warsaw was built too.
timeline.zh: 巴黎镭研究所由巴黎大学与巴斯德研究所共同建立，她领导物理化学实验室；此后又持续募款、推动华沙镭研究所建成。

timeline.en: Equipped and organised more than twenty mobile X-ray vehicles and around two hundred fixed radiological posts, went to the front herself, and trained the operators; over a million wounded men were imaged by these units during the war.
timeline.zh: 组织装备20 多辆移动 X 光车与约 200 处固定放射设施，并亲赴前线、培训放射技术人员；战时有超过一百万名伤员接受了这些设施的影像诊断。

timeline.en: Toured the United States raising money: American women gave a dollar at a time until they had the hundred thousand needed to buy her one gram of radium, which President Harding handed her at the White House — an early model of public crowdfunding for science.
timeline.zh: 赴美巡回募款，由美国女性一美元一美元凑出十万美元为她买下一克镭，哈定总统在白宫亲手交给她——现代科研公众募款的雏形。

timeline.en: Served as vice-president of the League of Nations' International Committee on Intellectual Cooperation, alongside Einstein — the forerunner of today's UNESCO.
timeline.zh: 出任国际联盟「知识合作委员会」副主席（同僚有爱因斯坦）——今天联合国教科文组织的前身。

story.en:
She studied by candlelight after work because universities in Poland did not admit women. In Paris she lived on bread and chocolate.

She won the Nobel Prize in Physics, then again in Chemistry. When the French Academy still refused to admit women, she simply stopped applying.

She didn't need the room. She built her own.
story.zh:
因为波兰的大学不收女性，她下工后在烛光里自学。在巴黎，她靠面包和巧克力过活。

她先后摘得诺贝尔物理学奖与化学奖。当法兰西学院依然拒绝接纳女性时，她干脆不再申请。

她不需要那个房间。她自己造了一个。

intro.en: She published one of the earliest complete algorithms written specifically for a general-purpose computing machine — for an Analytical Engine that was never built. More importantly, she saw that a machine could operate on symbols, music and rules, not just arithmetic.
intro.zh: 她发表了最早专门为通用计算机器设计的完整算法之一——而那台分析机尚未建成。更重要的是，她看见机器可以处理符号、音乐和规则，而不只是做算术。

timeline.en: Met Babbage's Difference Engine at seventeen and understood it on the spot.
timeline.zh: 十七岁见到巴贝奇的差分机，当场就懂了。

timeline.en: Commissioned to translate Menabrea's French paper on the Analytical Engine, she appended seven notes (A–G) three times longer than the original — the substantive theory of the engine is hers, signed only "A.A.L."
timeline.zh: 受托翻译 Menabrea 关于分析机的法文论文，附上的七条译注（Note A–G）长度是原文的三倍——整篇分析机理论文献实际是她写的，署名只有「A.A.L.」。

timeline.en: Note G sets out the step table for computing Bernoulli numbers on the Analytical Engine, usually called the first published computer program. Babbage had written unpublished program drafts earlier, so "the first program ever" remains contested in both definition and attribution.
timeline.zh: Note G 中给出分析机计算伯努利数的步骤表，通常被称为第一个公开发表的计算机程序。巴贝奇此前写过未发表的程序草稿，因此“史上第一个程序”仍有定义与归属争议。

timeline.en: Foresaw that the machine could compose music and operate on symbols rather than numbers alone — the founding insight of general-purpose computing, a century early.
timeline.zh: 预见机器可以作曲、可以处理符号而不只是数字——通用计算的奠基性洞察，早了一个世纪。

timeline.en: Her step table explicitly uses loops and nested loops, showing how one set of operations repeats under a condition; that is closer to her real contribution to programming than calling the table "a formula."
timeline.zh: 她的步骤表清楚使用了循环与嵌套循环，展示同一组运算如何按条件重复；这比把表格笼统称为“一个公式”更接近她真正的程序设计贡献。

timeline.en: She also argued the engine could originate nothing — it could only do what we know how to order it to perform. Turing named this "Lady Lovelace's Objection" in 1950 and answered it directly, making it an early landmark in the debate on machine intelligence.
timeline.zh: 她同时指出分析机只能执行人类知道如何命令它完成的事情。图灵在 1950 年把这一观点称为“Lovelace 女爵的反对意见”并专门回应，使它成为机器智能讨论中的早期经典命题。

coda.en: Her notes were republished in 1953 and recognised as a founding document of computer science; in 1980 the US Department of Defense named its programming language Ada, standard MIL-STD-1815, after her year of birth.
coda.zh: 1953 年她的注释被重新出版并确认为计算机科学的奠基文献；1980 年美国国防部将其编程语言命名为「Ada」，标准编号 MIL-STD-1815，取自她的生年。

story.en:
She saw what Babbage's machine could become before he did. She wrote programs for a computer that wouldn't be built for another hundred years.

She died at 36, largely unrecognized. Her notes were rediscovered in the 1950s and became foundational to computer science.

Being early is indistinguishable from being wrong — until it isn't. The work is still the work.
story.zh:
她比巴贝奇本人更早看见那台机器的未来。她为一台一百年后才会被造出来的计算机写下了程序。

她三十六岁去世，几乎无人知晓。她的注记在二十世纪五十年代被重新发现，成为计算机科学的基石。

太早，看起来和错了没有区别——直到时间站到你这边。而工作本身，始终作数。

intro.en: Mathematician, astronomer and teacher of Neoplatonic philosophy. None of her writing survives as an independent text, but ancient catalogues, letters from her students and traces in later manuscripts show she helped edit and expound the most important mathematical and astronomical works of her time.
intro.zh: 数学家、天文学家与新柏拉图主义哲学教师。她的著作已不以独立文本存世，但古代目录、学生书信和后来的文本痕迹显示，她参与整理并讲解了当时最重要的数学与天文学著作。

timeline.en: Taught by her father Theon, a mathematician, she later formed her own Neoplatonic teaching circle in Alexandria. The surviving evidence is not enough to show she formally "took over" any institution with a fixed establishment.
timeline.zh: 受教于数学家父亲 Theon，后来在亚历山大形成自己的新柏拉图主义教学圈；现有证据不足以证明她正式“接掌”了一所有固定建制的学院。

timeline.en: Lectured publicly on mathematics and astronomy; students came from across the Mediterranean to study under a woman.
timeline.zh: 公开讲授数学与天文学；学生从地中海各地赶来，只为跟一位女性学习。

timeline.en: Ancient sources credit her with commentaries on Diophantus's Arithmetica and Apollonius's Conics, and she may have worked on Book III of Theon's commentary on the Almagest. Some of it may survive inside later copies, but how much remains a scholarly argument.
timeline.zh: 古代资料把丢番图《算术》与阿波罗尼奥斯《圆锥曲线论》的注释归于她；她也可能参与修订 Theon 的《至大论》第三卷注。部分内容或保存在后来的抄本中，但具体范围仍是学术争论。

timeline.en: Guided her student Synesius in building a plane astrolabe; another letter asks her to have a hydrometer made to his description. The evidence supports her fluency with these instruments, not their invention or improvement.
timeline.zh: 指导学生 Synesius 制作平面星盘；另一封信请她按描述制作比重计。证据支持她熟悉这些仪器，但不支持“发明”或“改良”它们。

timeline.en: Became a public intellectual with real political weight in Alexandria — the prefect Orestes came to her for counsel, and her students included men who later became bishops.
timeline.zh: 成为亚历山大有实际政治分量的公共知识人——总督 Orestes 会前来征询她的意见，她的门生中有后来成为主教的人。

timeline.en: Killed by a Christian mob during the political and religious conflict between the prefect Orestes and Bishop Cyril. Ancient historians saw her as the obstacle to reconciliation between the two; a conflict this tangled should not be flattened into "science versus religion."
timeline.zh: 在总督 Orestes 与主教 Cyril 的政治及宗教冲突中，被一群基督徒暴民杀害。古代史家把她视为阻碍双方和解的人物；不能把复杂冲突简化为单一的“科学对宗教”。

sources.en: UCL, Women in the History of Science
sources.zh: UCL《Women in the History of Science》史料集

story.en:
She taught mathematics and astronomy in the open streets of Alexandria — a woman lecturing in public when women were not permitted to speak in civic spaces.

She was murdered for refusing to be silent.

What you carry feels lonely because it is. Most people who change things do it in rooms where no one else believes yet.
story.zh:
她在亚历山大城的街头讲授数学与天文——在女性不被允许公开发言的时代，一个女人当众讲学。

她因拒绝沉默而被杀害。

你背负的东西让你感到孤独，因为它确实孤独。大多数改变世界的人，都是在一个还没有人相信的房间里开始的。

intro.en: The only woman in Chinese history to take the throne formally under the title of Emperor. She widened the examination system, promoted new officials, and cultivated Buddhism and state ritual — and she purged her opponents through informants and cruel magistrates. Her achievements cannot be understood with the cost of that power left out.
intro.zh: 中国历史上唯一以“皇帝”名号正式即位的女性。她扩展科举、重用新官僚、经营佛教与国家仪式，也以告密制度和酷吏清洗反对者；理解她的成就，不能省略权力的代价。

timeline.en: Entered the palace at about fourteen as a junior consort of Emperor Taizong.
timeline.zh: 约十四岁入宫，为太宗才人。

timeline.en: With Gaozong gravely ill, she began governing in fact — reading memorials and deciding policy from behind the screen.
timeline.zh: 高宗病重，她开始实际执政——批阅奏章、垂帘决策。

timeline.en: Issued her twelve-point programme: lighter taxes and corvée, support for farming and sericulture, an end to campaigning.
timeline.zh: 颁建言十二事：轻徭薄赋、劝农桑、息兵。

timeline.en: With Gaozong she funded the Vairocana Buddha at Fengxian Temple in the Longmen Grottoes — an inscription records the empress contributing twenty thousand strings of "cosmetics money" — and later used Buddhist texts such as the Great Cloud Sutra to build the legitimacy of her reign.
timeline.zh: 与高宗共同资助龙门石窟奉先寺卢舍那大佛，碑刻记载皇后助“脂粉钱二万贯”；此后又借《大云经》等佛教资源建立称帝的合法性。

timeline.en: Commissioned the Biographies of Exemplary Women, Guidelines for Ministers, Domestic Norms Past and Present, and an agricultural manual distributed nationwide as a yardstick for assessing local officials; she also introduced more than ten newly coined characters used across the empire. She understood that the power to name things has to be built.
timeline.zh: 敕撰《列女传》《臣轨》《古今内范》《兆人本业记》（农书，颁行天下作为地方官考课依据）；并造「则天文字」十余个新字行于全国。她很清楚话语权是要自己造的。

timeline.en: Completed the Mingtang in Luoyang. The Old Book of Tang gives its height as 294 chi, roughly 88 metres in modern terms; it was an exceptionally large timber ritual hall, though "tallest in history" cannot be established strictly from surviving evidence.
timeline.zh: 建成洛阳明堂（万象神宫）。《旧唐书》记高二百九十四尺，现代换算约 88 米；它是当时规模极大的木构礼制建筑，但“历代最高”无法由现存证据严格证明。

timeline.en: Personally examined candidates in the palace courtyard at Luoyang, an early form of what became the palace examination; in 690 she took the throne and renamed the dynasty Zhou, the only woman in Chinese history to reign formally as Emperor.
timeline.zh: 亲自在洛阳殿廷策问贡士，发展出后来殿试的早期形式；690 年称帝、改国号为周，成为中国历史上唯一正式以皇帝名号即位的女性。

timeline.en: Installed bronze petition boxes to encourage denunciations nationwide and employed cruel magistrates such as Lai Junchen to interrogate and execute political enemies and members of the Tang house. It broke the aristocratic opposition and produced years of political terror; later she executed some of those magistrates and wound the system back.
timeline.zh: 设置铜匦鼓励全国告密，并任用来俊臣等酷吏审讯、处决政敌和唐宗室。它帮助她摧毁门阀反对力量，也制造了持续数年的政治恐怖；后期她处死部分酷吏、收缩这一体系。

timeline.en: Widened the examination and recommendation channels, raised the standing of officials who entered by examination, and brought in scholars from outside the northwestern aristocracy. Di Renjie, Yao Chong and Song Jing, whom she promoted, went on serving the restored Tang.
timeline.zh: 扩大科举与荐举渠道，提高进士出身官员地位，让更多非西北门阀背景的士人进入政府；她重用的狄仁杰、姚崇、宋璟后来继续服务于唐朝。

timeline.en: Sent Wang Xiaojie to retake the Four Garrisons of Anxi, re-established the Anxi Protectorate at Kucha, and reopened the Silk Road.
timeline.zh: 遣王孝杰收复安西四镇，重设安西都护府于龟兹，重新打通丝绸之路。

timeline.en: Created the military examination and ordered civil and military officials to recommend military talent — opening an official career to soldiers regardless of birth.
timeline.zh: 始创武举，下诏鼓励文武官员举荐军事人才——为不问出身的武人打开了仕途。

timeline.en: Forced to abdicate, she still arranged her own afterlife as Empress Zetian, ordering before her death that her imperial title be dropped and that she be buried with Gaozong at Qianling — a last decision about how she would be recorded.
timeline.zh: 被迫退位后仍以「则天大圣皇后」身份安排身后事，去世前下令去帝号、归葬乾陵——最后一次自己决定自己怎么被记载。

coda.en: A wordless stele was raised at Qianling when she was buried with Gaozong in 706. The line about "leaving the verdict to later generations" is a later attribution with no basis in Tang sources.
coda.zh: 706 年与高宗合葬时立无字碑于乾陵。「留给后人评说」的说法出自后世附会，唐代史料中并无依据。

sources.en: Old Book of Tang, on the Mingtang

story.en:
She entered the imperial court as a concubine at fourteen. She left it as Emperor.

For fifty years she outmaneuvered every man who tried to remove her — through the kind of patience that looks like stillness from the outside and feels like fire from within.

The people who call your ambition dangerous are the ones who know exactly how far it will take you.
story.zh:
她十四岁以妃嫔身份入宫，离开时已是皇帝。

五十年间，她胜过了每一个试图除掉她的男人——靠的是那种从外面看像静止、从里面看像火焰的耐心。

说你的野心危险的人，恰恰是最清楚它能带你走多远的人。

intro.en: She turned bodily experience, Mexican identity and political conviction into subjects of modern art. The fifty-five or so self-portraits are only part of the work: she also painted still lifes, double portraits and political allegory, and built an international reputation through shows in New York, Paris and Mexico.
intro.zh: 她把身体经验、墨西哥身份与政治立场变成现代艺术的主题。约五十五幅自画像只是作品的一部分；她同时创作静物、双人像与政治寓言，并通过纽约、巴黎和墨西哥的展览建立起国际声誉。

timeline.en: Admitted to Mexico's National Preparatory School — thirty-five women among some two thousand students — where she studied natural sciences, intending to become a doctor.
timeline.zh: 考入墨西哥国立预科学校——约两千名学生中仅三十五名女生，主修自然科学，志向是当医生。

timeline.en: The bus she was riding collided with a streetcar, gravely injuring her spine, pelvis and right leg. Bedridden for long stretches, she took up painting in earnest.
timeline.zh: 她乘坐的公共汽车与有轨电车相撞，造成脊柱、骨盆和右腿等多处重伤；长期卧床期间，她系统投入绘画。

timeline.en: Painted Henry Ford Hospital, one of the earliest works in modern art to depict miscarriage, blood loss and bodily trauma directly, putting an experience rarely seen in public art at the centre of the picture.
timeline.zh: 画《Henry Ford Hospital》，成为现代艺术中很早直接表现流产、失血与身体创伤的作品之一，把少见于公共艺术的女性经验置于画面中心。

timeline.en: She and Rivera hosted the exiled Trotsky at the Blue House. She was involved in left politics for most of her life, though not continuously active inside the Mexican Communist Party at this point — she rejoined in 1948.
timeline.zh: 与里维拉在蓝屋接待流亡的托洛茨基；她长期参与左翼政治，但此时并非持续在墨西哥共产党党内活动，1948 年才重新入党。

timeline.en: First solo show in New York, followed by the Mexique exhibition in Paris. The French state bought The Frame, taking the work into the national collection, now at the Centre Pompidou; it is often recorded as the first twentieth-century Mexican painting the French national collection accepted.
timeline.zh: 在纽约举办首次个展，次年参加巴黎“Mexique”展。法国政府购入《The Frame》，作品进入国家收藏、现藏蓬皮杜中心；它常被记为法国国家收藏接纳的第一件二十世纪墨西哥绘画。

timeline.en: Breton folded her into Surrealist exhibitions and writing; she insisted afterwards, repeatedly, that her work came from her own reality rather than dreams — keeping deliberate distance from the European label.
timeline.zh: 布勒东把她纳入超现实主义展览与论述；她后来反复强调作品来自自身现实而不是梦境，主动与欧洲对她的分类保持距离。

timeline.en: Painted The Two Fridas, now among the most widely known self-portraits of the twentieth century.
timeline.zh: 画《两个弗里达》，成为二十世纪最广为人知的自画像之一。

timeline.en: Taught at the La Esmeralda art school; when pain kept her at home, the students who called themselves Los Fridos came to her house for class.
timeline.zh: 在 La Esmeralda 艺术学院任教；疼痛让她无法出门时，学生「Los Fridos」就到她家来上课。

timeline.en: Received a special honourable mention for Moses in the national arts and sciences prize administered by the presidency and the education ministry — not the top award, but significant national recognition in her lifetime.
timeline.zh: 以《Moses》获墨西哥总统府与公共教育部国家科学与艺术奖特别荣誉提名，并非该奖最高奖项；这仍是她生前获得的重要国家级认可。

timeline.en: Her first solo show in Mexico. Ordered to stay in bed, she had her four-poster bed carried into the gallery and received guests lying in it.
timeline.zh: 墨西哥首次个展。医嘱卧床，她让人把自己的四柱床抬进画廊，躺在床上迎客。

story.en:
At eighteen, a streetcar accident shattered her spine, pelvis, and leg. She spent months in a body cast — so she had a mirror mounted above her bed and began painting the only subject available: herself.

Fifty-five self-portraits. Not vanity — testimony. Pain made visible, grief made beautiful, identity made undeniable.

Her last painting is inscribed: "Viva la vida." Long live life. She meant it.
story.zh:
十八岁，电车事故击碎了她的脊柱、骨盆和腿。她在石膏里躺了几个月——于是在床顶装了一面镜子，开始画唯一能画的对象：她自己。

五十五幅自画像。不是自恋，是证词。把疼痛画给人看，把悲伤画成美，把「我是谁」画得无可辩驳。

她最后一幅画上写着：Viva la vida——生命万岁。她是认真的。

intro.en: From planting trees she built a method that joined environmental repair, income for women and democratic participation. In the year she died the Green Belt Movement reported more than fifty-one million trees planted; she also carried environmental citizenship into parliament and government.
intro.zh: 她从种树建立了一套把环境修复、女性收入与民主参与连在一起的组织方法。绿带运动在她去世当年报告累计种植超过五千一百万棵树；她也把环境公民运动带进了议会与政府。

timeline.en: Became the first woman in East or Central Africa to earn a doctorate.
timeline.zh: 成为东非与中非第一位取得博士学位的女性。

timeline.en: Appointed head of veterinary anatomy at the University of Nairobi, then associate professor the following year — the university's first woman in each post.
timeline.zh: 出任内罗毕大学兽医解剖学系主任，次年升任副教授；她分别成为该校第一位女性系主任和副教授。

timeline.en: Founded the Green Belt Movement: paying rural women to plant trees — income, ecology and dignity in a single act.
timeline.zh: 创办绿带运动：付酬让农村女性种树——收入、生态与尊严一次完成。

timeline.en: Won the Right Livelihood Award, the "alternative Nobel" — twenty years before the Peace Prize.
timeline.zh: 获 Right Livelihood Award（「另类诺贝尔奖」）——比诺贝尔和平奖早二十年。

timeline.en: Exported the Green Belt model to more than a dozen African countries, among them Tanzania, Uganda and Malawi.
timeline.zh: 把绿带模式输出到坦桑尼亚、乌干达、马拉维等十余个非洲国家。

timeline.en: Led the fight that stopped a sixty-storey tower in Nairobi's Uhuru Park — and beat the regime.
timeline.zh: 领导抗争，阻止了内罗毕乌呼鲁公园的六十层高楼——她赢了这个政权。

timeline.en: Supported and joined the hunger strike by mothers of political prisoners at Uhuru Park's Freedom Corner, and was injured when police broke it up. The mothers moved into a church and kept protesting until the last of those prisoners were released in January 1993.
timeline.zh: 支持并参与乌呼鲁公园「自由角」政治犯母亲绝食抗议，在警方驱散中受伤。母亲们随后转入教堂继续抗议，直至 1993 年 1 月最后一批相关政治犯获释。

timeline.en: Entered presidential and parliamentary politics, trying to combine environment, anti-corruption and democratic reform into a formal platform. The campaign failed, but it built the national experience behind her 2002 win.
timeline.zh: 进入总统与议会选举政治，尝试把环境、反腐败与民主改革组合成正式政治纲领；竞选没有成功，却为 2002 年当选议员积累了全国政治经验。

timeline.en: Elected to parliament with 98% of the vote, and made assistant minister for environment, natural resources and wildlife the next year — she took the street movement inside the state.
timeline.zh: 以 98% 得票率当选国会议员，次年出任环境、自然资源与野生动物部副部长——她把街头运动带进了体制。

timeline.en: Won the Nobel Peace Prize, the first African woman to do so. The Nobel Committee recorded over thirty million trees planted by the movement at the time; the fifty-million-plus figure is the cumulative total by 2011.
timeline.zh: 获诺贝尔和平奖，成为第一位获该奖的非洲女性。诺贝尔委员会当时记载绿带运动已推动种植三千多万棵树；五千万以上是此后到 2011 年的累计数字。

timeline.en: Published the memoir Unbowed. The UN Billion Tree Campaign was directly inspired and driven by her — when a company offered to plant a million trees, she replied that what was really needed was a billion. The campaign has since planted some 12.5 billion.
timeline.zh: 出版回忆录《Unbowed》；联合国「十亿棵树运动」由她直接启发并推动——有企业说要种一百万棵，她回：「很好，但我们真正需要的是十亿棵。」该运动累计种下约 125 亿棵树。

story.en:
When the men in power called her crazy and divorced, beat and jailed her, she kept planting trees — and paying rural women to plant them too.

Fifty million trees. Thousands of women earning their own income for the first time. A dictatorship's grip loosened one seedling at a time.

She won the Nobel Peace Prize. "It's the little things citizens do. That's what will make the difference."
story.zh:
当掌权的男人们骂她疯了、打她、关押她时，她继续种树——并付钱请乡村妇女一起种。

五千万棵树。成千上万的女性第一次有了自己的收入。独裁的铁腕，被一株一株的树苗撬松。

她获得了诺贝尔和平奖。「是公民做的那些小事。改变世界的正是这些。」

intro.en: Born into slavery, she renamed herself and then spoke until the country heard her. She could not read or write, and Dutch was her first language; her words changed thousands of minds.
intro.zh: 生于奴隶制，她给自己重新取名，然后一直说到这个国家听见为止。她不识字，母语是荷兰语；她的话让成千上万人改变了想法。

timeline.en: Walked to freedom carrying her infant daughter, a year before New York's emancipation took effect.
timeline.zh: 带着襁褓中的女儿走向自由，比纽约州废奴生效早了一年。

timeline.en: Sued a white man to recover her son Peter, sold illegally into Alabama — and won. One of the first Black women to win such a case in an American court.
timeline.zh: 起诉一名白人，追回被非法卖去阿拉巴马的儿子 Peter——并胜诉。美国法庭上最早赢得此类诉讼的黑人女性之一。

timeline.en: Renamed herself Sojourner Truth and began travelling the country to preach it.
timeline.zh: 为自己重新取名 Sojourner Truth，开始走遍全国传讲它。

timeline.en: Published The Narrative of Sojourner Truth, dictated to Olive Gilbert, and sold it herself at meetings to live on — turning her autobiography into both a political instrument and an income.
timeline.zh: 口述出版《The Narrative of Sojourner Truth》（由 Olive Gilbert 记录），并在集会上亲自卖书养活自己——她把自传变成了政治工具与生计。

timeline.en: Spoke extemporaneously at the women's rights convention in Akron, Ohio, holding race, labour and women's rights inside a single argument — an early landmark of what would later be called intersectional feminism.
timeline.zh: 在俄亥俄州阿克伦妇女权利大会上即席发言，把种族、劳动与女性权利放在同一论证中，成为后来所谓交叉性女性主义的重要早期文本。

timeline.en: Sold photographic portraits of herself to fund her speaking tours and her living, printing on them: "I sell the shadow to support the substance." She took control of how a Black woman intellectual was pictured, and circulated it.
timeline.zh: 销售自己的肖像照片为巡回演讲与生活筹款，并在照片上印下“我出售影子，以支持实体”。她主动控制并传播一个黑人女性公共知识人的视觉形象。

timeline.en: Recruited Black soldiers for the Union and gathered supplies for them, and worked among the freed people in Washington; her 1864 meeting with Lincoln was one moment in that sustained work.
timeline.zh: 为黑人联邦军募兵、筹集补给，并在华盛顿为获释者工作；1864 年与林肯会面只是这段持续行动中的一个节点。

timeline.en: Employed by the National Freedmen's Relief Association at Freedman's Village in Washington, training freed people in skills and placing them in work.
timeline.zh: 受聘于全国自由民救济协会，在华盛顿 Freedman's Village 为获释者做技能培训与就业安置。

timeline.en: Kept riding Washington's streetcars to force the desegregation rules to be enforced; after a conductor assaulted her she brought assault charges and won the case — not a general suit against the company.
timeline.zh: 持续乘坐华盛顿有轨电车推动执行反隔离规定；一名车掌暴力阻拦她后，她提出袭击指控并赢得案件，而不是笼统“起诉整家公司”。

timeline.en: At the American Equal Rights Association convention she opposed simply ordering Black male and female suffrage one before the other, asking where Black women would be left — a crucial first-hand witness to the movement's internal conflict.
timeline.zh: 在美国平等权利协会大会上反对把黑人男性与女性选举权简单排成先后，追问黑人女性会被置于何处；这是权利运动内部冲突的重要一手见证。

timeline.en: Petitioned Congress to grant western land to freed Black people, touring to gather signatures. It failed, but it stands among the earliest claims for Black land reparations.
timeline.zh: 向国会请愿为获释黑人划拨西部土地，四处演讲征集签名。方案未通过，但这是最早的黑人土地赔偿主张之一。

story.en:
She was born Isabella. At forty-six she renamed herself Sojourner Truth — because she was going to travel the land and tell the truth.

She couldn't read or write. Her speeches moved thousands. She stood in rooms that wanted her silent and spoke anyway.

"I am not going to die, I'm going home like a shooting star." She knew exactly who she was. That's where power begins.
story.zh:
她出生时叫伊莎贝拉。四十六岁那年，她给自己改名 Sojourner Truth——因为她要走遍这片土地，把真相讲出来。

她不会读写。她的演讲撼动千万人。那些房间希望她沉默，她偏偏开口。

「我不会死去，我会像流星一样回家。」她清楚地知道自己是谁。力量正是从这里开始的。

intro.en: She did foundational work in three fields: carbon materials, DNA, and virus structure. Photo 51 was one of the key pieces of evidence for the double helix. The Nobel went to Watson, Crick and Wilkins four years after her death, and the prize is not awarded posthumously — so how the committee would otherwise have divided it cannot simply be asserted.
intro.zh: 她在碳材料、DNA 与病毒结构三个领域都做出了奠基性工作。Photo 51 是双螺旋模型的关键证据之一；她去世四年后，诺奖授予沃森、克里克与威尔金斯，而诺贝尔奖不作身后授奖，因此不能简单断言评委会本应如何分配。

timeline.en: Completed her doctorate on the physical chemistry of coal; her work on pore structure became the basis for wartime gas-mask filter material.
timeline.zh: 完成关于煤的物理化学博士论文；她对孔隙结构的研究成为战时防毒面具滤材的基础。

timeline.en: Published the distinction between graphitising and non-graphitising carbons in the Proceedings of the Royal Society, and built a model of how graphite crystallites develop. The classification remains an important historical frame for understanding carbon structure; modern batteries and carbon fibre were not her invention alone.
timeline.zh: 提出石墨化碳与非石墨化碳的分类（《皇家学会会刊》），并建立石墨微晶演变模型。这套分类仍是理解碳材料结构的重要历史框架；现代电池与碳纤维并非由她单独“发明”。

timeline.en: With the graduate student Raymond Gosling she designed and tuned a humidity-controlled X-ray apparatus, and distinguished the wet B form of DNA from the drier A form.
timeline.zh: 与研究生 Raymond Gosling 设计、调试可控制湿度的 X 射线装置，并区分 DNA 的湿态 B 型与较干燥的 A 型。

timeline.en: Her doctoral student Gosling, under her direction, took Photo 51 — later called one of the most beautiful scientific photographs ever made.
timeline.zh: 她的博士生 Gosling 在她指导下拍下 Photo 51——后来被称为史上最美的科学照片之一。

timeline.en: While building their model, Watson and Crick saw two sets of her unpublished data: Photo 51, shown by Wilkins without her consent, and an internal MRC report passed on via Perutz. Her paper with Gosling appeared in the same issue of Nature, where the running order made her contribution look like corroboration of the model.
timeline.zh: 沃森与克里克建模时接触到两类她未公开的数据：Wilkins 未经她同意展示的 Photo 51，以及经由 Perutz 传递的 MRC 内部报告。她与 Gosling 的论文同刊于《Nature》，其排序让贡献在当时显得像模型的佐证。

timeline.en: Led a team at Birkbeck on tobacco mosaic virus and showed that the RNA sits inside the protein helix; the twenty-one virus papers she and her team published were a foundation of structural virology.
timeline.zh: 在 Birkbeck 领导团队研究烟草花叶病毒，证明 RNA 位于蛋白质螺旋内部；她与团队发表的 21 篇病毒论文为结构病毒学奠定了重要基础。

timeline.en: Started her team on the structure of poliovirus. Her collaborator Aaron Klug carried the methods forward and won the 1982 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for crystallographic electron microscopy and nucleic acid–protein complexes.
timeline.zh: 带队启动脊髓灰质炎病毒结构研究。合作者 Aaron Klug 延续了相关结构生物学方法，并于 1982 年因晶体学电子显微镜和核酸—蛋白复合物研究获诺贝尔化学奖。

timeline.en: Conceived a large model of tobacco mosaic virus for the Brussels World's Fair; after her death the team built and exhibited it from her findings.
timeline.zh: 为布鲁塞尔世博会构思大型烟草花叶病毒模型；她去世后，团队依照研究成果完成并展出模型。

coda.en: She died in Chelsea in April 1958, aged thirty-seven. Her epitaph reads: "Scientist. Her research and discoveries on viruses remain of lasting benefit to mankind."
coda.zh: 1958 年 4 月卒于切尔西，年三十七。墓志铭：「科学家。她对病毒的研究与发现将长久造福人类。」

story.en:
She did not guess at DNA's structure. She photographed it — with a camera she built herself, in conditions she controlled to a fraction of a percent humidity.

Photo 51 was shown to Watson without her knowledge. The double helix was published with a footnote. She moved to Birkbeck, studied viruses, published sixty papers, and never wasted a day on bitterness.

The work is the work. It does not need anyone's permission to be true.
story.zh:
她没有猜测DNA的结构。她拍下了它——用她亲手搭建的相机，在她精确控制到百分之几湿度的条件下。

第51号照片在她不知情的情况下被展示给沃森。双螺旋以脚注的方式发表。她转去伯贝克学院，研究病毒，发表六十篇论文，从未把一天浪费在怨恨上。

工作就是工作。它不需要任何人的许可就是真理。

intro.en: She moved British women's suffrage from lobbying to highly organised direct action: founding organisations, running newspapers, raising money, touring to speak, and accepting the political risk of prison and hunger strikes. She was a central leader of a collective movement, not the sole inventor of its every tactic.
intro.zh: 她把英国妇女参政运动从游说推向高度组织化的直接行动：建立组织、经营媒体、筹款、巡回演讲，并接受监禁和绝食带来的政治风险。她是集体运动的重要领导者，而不是所有策略的单一发明人。

timeline.en: Co-founded the Women's Franchise League with Richard Pankhurst, Elizabeth Wolstenholme Elmy and others, putting the local-election vote for married women on the agenda; the law widened that right in 1894.
timeline.zh: 与 Richard Pankhurst、Elizabeth Wolstenholme Elmy 等人共同创办女性选举权同盟，把已婚女性的地方选举权纳入运动议程；1894 年法律扩大了这项权利。

timeline.en: Elected a Poor Law Guardian in Chorlton, where she reformed the workhouse's treatment of women and children. She had done the administrative work first.
timeline.zh: 当选 Chorlton 济贫院监事，任内改革了济贫院对女性与儿童的待遇。她是先做过实务官员的。

timeline.en: Founded the Women's Social and Political Union at 62 Nelson Street, Manchester, on a one-line platform: "Deeds, not words."
timeline.zh: 在曼彻斯特纳尔逊街 62 号创办妇女社会政治同盟（WSPU），纲领只有一句：「行动，不要言辞。」

timeline.en: With Emmeline and Frederick Pethick-Lawrence, the WSPU launched the paper Votes for Women, later replaced by The Suffragette as the official organ — making its own press part of the movement's infrastructure.
timeline.zh: WSPU 与 Emmeline、Frederick Pethick-Lawrence 共同建立机关报《Votes for Women》，后来又以《The Suffragette》为官方报纸，把自办媒体变成运动基础设施。

timeline.en: First arrested; told the court: "We are here not because we are law-breakers; we are here in our efforts to become law-makers."
timeline.zh: 首次被捕，在庭上宣称：「我们站在这里不是因为我们违法，而是因为我们要成为立法者。」

timeline.en: Sentenced to three years' penal servitude; released and re-arrested twelve times in one year under the Cat and Mouse Act as she starved herself, dropping below forty kilos — she made her own body a political problem the government could not process.
timeline.zh: 被判三年苦役；一年之内因绝食被反复放出又抓回十二次（《猫鼠法案》），体重掉到不足四十公斤——她把自己的身体变成了政府无法处理的政治问题。

timeline.en: The WSPU organised a Right to Serve march of some thirty thousand people demanding wider wartime employment for women. It helped open munitions work, though women's mass entry into industry also came from labour shortage and other organisations.
timeline.zh: 与 WSPU 组织约三万人的“服务权”游行，要求政府扩大女性战时就业；它推动了军工岗位开放，但女性大规模进入工业也由劳动力短缺和多方组织共同造成。

timeline.en: Years of movement pressure contributed to the Representation of the People Act: the vote for women over thirty who met a property qualification, about 8.4 million of them; the same year women became eligible to stand for the Commons.
timeline.zh: 长期运动参与促成《人民代表法》：三十岁以上且符合财产资格的女性获得选举权，约八百四十万人；同年女性取得竞选下议院资格。

timeline.en: Selected as the Conservative parliamentary candidate for Whitechapel. She had won women the right to stand — then went and used it.
timeline.zh: 获选为白教堂选区保守党议会候选人。她争到了女性参选权，然后自己去用了它。

timeline.en: Died in Hampstead on 14 June. The Equal Franchise Act — the vote for all women over twenty-one — passed on 2 July, eighteen days later.
timeline.zh: 6 月 14 日卒于汉普斯特德。《平等选举权法》——二十一岁以上全体女性投票权——于 7 月 2 日通过，十八天后。

story.en:
For forty years, women asked politely. They wrote letters. They held meetings. Nothing changed.

So Emmeline Pankhurst founded the WSPU with three words: 'Deeds, not words.' They broke windows. They were arrested, force-fed, imprisoned, and they came back. Every single time.

She died eighteen days before the full vote passed. She did not need to see it. She had already felt it coming.
story.zh:
四十年间，女性们礼貌地请求。她们写信。她们开会。什么都没有改变。

于是埃梅琳·潘克赫斯特创立了妇女社会政治联盟，只有三个字：「行动，不是空话。」她们砸碎窗户。她们被捕、被强制灌食、被监禁，她们每一次都回来了。

她在全面投票权通过的十八天前去世。她不需要亲眼看到。她早已感觉到它要来了。

intro.en: The first woman to head the government of a Muslim-majority country, twice prime minister of Pakistan. She restored some civil liberties and built institutions and public health programmes for women; both of her governments were also dismissed by the president before term, amid lasting disputes over governance and corruption.
intro.zh: 她是第一位出任穆斯林人口占多数国家政府首脑的女性，两度担任巴基斯坦总理。她恢复部分公民自由、推动女性机构与公共卫生项目；两届政府也都在任期结束前被总统解散，并长期伴随治理与腐败争议。

timeline.en: Elected President of the Oxford Union — the first Asian woman to hold the post.
timeline.zh: 当选牛津辩论社主席——第一位担任此职的亚洲女性。

timeline.en: Her father Zulfikar Ali Bhutto was hanged after a trial a former US Attorney General called a kangaroo court.
timeline.zh: 父亲布托在一场被前美国司法部长称为「袋鼠法庭」的审判后被绞死。

timeline.en: Became chair of the Pakistan Peoples Party while in exile, directing the campaign against Zia from London.
timeline.zh: 流亡中出任巴基斯坦人民党主席，从伦敦遥控组织反齐亚运动。

timeline.en: Returned home to an enormous welcome in Lahore; estimates ran from several hundred thousand to over a million, marking her as the national leader of the anti-military opposition.
timeline.zh: 回国，在拉合尔受到规模巨大的欢迎；报道估计从数十万到逾百万人不等，显示她已成为反军政府阵营的全国性领导者。

timeline.en: The PPP became the largest party in parliament and formed a coalition; at thirty-five she was sworn in as prime minister — the first woman to lead the government of a Muslim-majority country.
timeline.zh: 人民党赢得议会最大党地位并组成联合政府；她三十五岁宣誓就任总理，成为首位领导穆斯林人口占多数国家政府的女性。

timeline.en: Lifted some restrictions on the press and political activity, released political prisoners, and brought Pakistan back into the Commonwealth; the army and presidency kept strong powers, which limited how far reform could go.
timeline.zh: 解除部分新闻与政治活动限制、释放政治犯，并带巴基斯坦重返英联邦；军方与总统保留强大权力，使改革幅度受到限制。

timeline.en: Established the First Women Bank; her second government opened Pakistan's first all-women police stations in 1994 and pushed women into the senior judiciary and family courts.
timeline.zh: 设立第一妇女银行；第二届政府于 1994 年开办首批全女性警察局，并推动女性进入高等司法与家庭法院。

timeline.en: Both governments were dismissed early by the president, on grounds including misgovernment, corruption and deteriorating security. Some charges involved her husband and political network; later verdicts and inquiries did not all agree.
timeline.zh: 两届政府都被总统提前解散，理由包括治理失当、腐败与治安恶化；相关指控部分涉及其丈夫和政治网络，后来判决与调查结果并不完全一致。

timeline.en: The PPP again became the largest party and formed a coalition, returning her to office as prime minister for a second term.
timeline.zh: 人民党再次取得议会最大党地位并联合组阁，她第二次出任总理（1993–1996）。

timeline.en: Drove a national polio vaccination programme reaching tens of millions of children.
timeline.zh: 推动全国小儿麻痹疫苗接种计划，覆盖数千万儿童。

timeline.en: Returned from exile to Karachi, where two bombs at her welcome rally that night killed at least 139 people, by some counts around 180. She gave the next day's speech as planned.
timeline.zh: 流亡归国抵达卡拉奇，当晚两枚炸弹在欢迎集会上炸死至少 139 人（一说约 180 人）。她照常发表了第二天的演讲。

timeline.en: Assassinated on 27 December in Rawalpindi after addressing a rally. She was fifty-four.
timeline.zh: 12 月 27 日在拉瓦尔品第演讲后遇刺身亡，终年五十四岁。

sources.zh: 巴基斯坦政府新闻信息部

sources.en: Reporting on the 1994 women's police stations

story.en:
Her father was hanged. Her brothers were killed. She spent years in solitary confinement and years in exile. The night she returned to Pakistan, a bomb killed 180 of her supporters.

She gave the next speech anyway. And the one after that.

Fear is what the people trying to stop you are counting on. She decided what mattered more.
story.zh:
她的父亲被绞死。她的兄弟被杀害。她在单独监禁中度过数年，又在流亡中度过数年。她回到巴基斯坦的那个夜晚，一枚炸弹炸死了她的180名支持者。

她照样发表了下一场演讲。以及再下一场。

恐惧，是那些试图阻止你的人赖以为凭的东西。她选择了更重要的事。

intro.en: She escaped slavery and went back to Maryland again and again to bring others out; later she built intelligence networks for the Union army and helped plan and guide the Combahee River raid. Underground transport, military scouting, social care and suffrage organising were one continuous public life.
intro.zh: 她从奴隶制中逃出，又多次返回马里兰带人离开；此后为联邦军建立情报网络，并参与策划和引导库姆比河突袭。她把地下交通、军事侦察、社会照护与妇女选举权组织连成了一生的公共事业。

timeline.en: Escaped alone from Maryland to Pennsylvania. No exact route survives; the North Star, Underground Railroad contacts and Quaker safe houses were all plausibly used, and later summaries should not be written up as a complete itinerary.
timeline.zh: 独自从马里兰逃到宾夕法尼亚。确切路线没有保存下来；北极星、地下交通联系人与贵格会安全屋是可能使用的方式，不宜把后来的概括写成完整行程记录。

timeline.en: After the Fugitive Slave Act passed she worked with the Underground Railroad network to take some of those she freed onward to Canada, establishing a base at St. Catharines, Ontario.
timeline.zh: 《逃亡奴隶法》通过后，她与地下交通网络合作，把部分被解救者继续带到加拿大，并在安大略圣凯瑟琳斯建立生活据点。

timeline.en: Returned to Maryland at least thirteen times, personally leading out about seventy enslaved people. She never lost one.
timeline.zh: 返回马里兰至少十三次，亲自带出约七十名被奴役者。从未丢过一个人。

timeline.en: Brought her parents from Maryland to Canada in 1857; in 1859 bought seven acres near Auburn, New York on credit from William Seward, giving her family a permanent base while the Fugitive Slave Act still stood.
timeline.zh: 1857 年把父母从马里兰带到加拿大；1859 年又向 William Seward 赊购纽约州奥本附近七英亩地，使家人在《逃亡奴隶法》仍有效时拥有长期据点。

timeline.en: Conspired with John Brown over the Harpers Ferry raid and recruited men for him. Brown called her "General Tubman."
timeline.zh: 与 John Brown 共谋哈珀斯渡口起义并为他招募人手。Brown 称她为「Tubman 将军」。

timeline.en: Served the Union army as a civilian nurse, cook, guide, scout and intelligence organiser, building a network in South Carolina through local Black people; she held no formal rank.
timeline.zh: 以平民身份为联邦军担任护士、厨师、向导、侦察员与情报组织者，在南卡罗来纳借助当地黑人建立情报网络；她当时没有正式军衔。

timeline.en: Helped plan and guide the Combahee River raid on intelligence from her network of Black scouts; Colonel James Montgomery commanded the troops and three gunboats carried away more than seven hundred people. She is widely regarded as the first woman to lead an American military operation.
timeline.zh: 参与策划并引导库姆比河突袭，情报来自她和黑人侦察员网络；Colonel James Montgomery 指挥参战部队，三艘炮艇帮助解放七百多人。她被广泛视为首位领导美国军事行动的女性。

timeline.en: Petitioned for decades over pay and pension for her Union service. In 1899 Congress raised the pension she drew as a soldier's widow to twenty dollars a month, citing her own nursing work; she never received a full pension in her own right.
timeline.zh: 为联邦军服务报酬与抚恤持续申诉数十年。1899 年国会把她作为退伍军人遗孀领取的养老金提高到每月二十美元，并提到她本人的护理服务；她始终没有获得一份完整、独立的军役养老金。

timeline.en: Bought the adjoining property to house impoverished elderly Black people; the same year she attended the founding convention of the National Association of Colored Women, and she spoke and organised for suffrage for years.
timeline.zh: 购下相邻地产，为收容贫困黑人老人做准备；同年出席全国有色妇女协会成立大会，并长期参与妇女选举权演讲与组织。

timeline.en: Transferred the land to the AME Zion Church and worked with it to establish the Harriet Tubman Home for the Aged, which took in its first residents in 1908.
timeline.zh: 把土地转交非洲卫理公会锡安教会管理，合作建立Harriet Tubman 老年之家；该机构 1908 年正式接收老人。

coda.en: She died in Auburn in 1913, about ninety-one years old, and was buried at Fort Hill Cemetery with military honours.
coda.zh: 1913 年卒于奥本，约九十一岁，以军礼葬于 Fort Hill 公墓。

story.en:
She crossed into Pennsylvania alone, on foot, in the dark. She looked at her hands to see if she was the same person. There was such a glory over everything.

Then she went back. Thirteen times. Ninety miles through swamp and darkness, with dogs behind her and the North Star above. She never lost a single passenger.

I never ran my train off the track, she said. And she meant it.
story.zh:
她独自一人，徒步，在黑暗中越过边界进入宾夕法尼亚。她看着自己的双手，想确认自己是否还是同一个人。一切之上笼罩着一种光辉。

然后她回去了。十三次。九十英里，穿过沼泽和黑暗，身后是猎犬，头顶是北极星。她从未丢失过一名乘客。

我的列车从未脱轨，她说。她是认真的。

intro.en: At twenty-one she passed France's hardest philosophy examination, placing second only to Sartre and the youngest ever to do it. Then she wrote the sentence that split the century in two: "One is not born, but rather becomes, a woman."
intro.zh: 二十一岁，她通过了法国最难的哲学教师资格会考，仅次于萨特，且是史上最年轻。然后她写下把二十世纪劈成两半的那句话：「女人不是天生的，而是变成的。」

timeline.en: Passed the agrégation in philosophy at twenty-one — the youngest candidate ever, and only the eighth woman to pass.
timeline.zh: 二十一岁通过哲学教师资格会考——史上最年轻的考生，也是第八位通过的女性。

timeline.en: Published her first novel, She Came to Stay, working through existentialist freedom and the problem of the other in fiction.
timeline.zh: 出版第一部小说《女宾》，用小说形式处理存在主义的自由与他者问题。

timeline.en: Co-founded Les Temps modernes with Sartre, Merleau-Ponty, Raymond Aron and others, editing and writing for it for decades; it became one of the most important intellectual journals of postwar France.
timeline.zh: 与萨特、梅洛-庞蒂、Raymond Aron 等人共同创办《现代》杂志，并长期参与编辑与写作；它成为战后法国最重要的思想刊物之一。

timeline.en: Published The Second Sex, arguing that womanhood is constructed rather than biological — the founding text of feminist philosophy.
timeline.zh: 出版《第二性》，论证女性身份不是生理而是建构——女性主义哲学的奠基文本。

timeline.en: Won the Prix Goncourt for The Mandarins.
timeline.zh: 以《名士风流》获龚古尔奖。

timeline.en: Published The Long March after visiting China, an extended account of the new state — and was criticised for indulgence toward the politics and social constraints of the Mao years. That limitation is part of her record as a public intellectual.
timeline.zh: 访华后出版《长征》，系统介绍新中国，也因对毛时代政治与社会约束过于宽容而受到批评；这份局限是她公共知识分子生涯的一部分。

timeline.en: Published Memoirs of a Dutiful Daughter, opening a four-volume memoir that treats her own formation, class and gendered socialisation as objects of analysis.
timeline.zh: 出版《端方淑女的回忆》，开启四卷回忆录，把个人成长、阶级与性别社会化同时作为分析对象。

timeline.en: Served on Russell's International War Crimes Tribunal on Vietnam.
timeline.zh: 出任罗素越战国际战犯法庭成员。

timeline.en: Published The Coming of Age, drawing together history, literature, economics and daily life to analyse how societies make the old into the other — a landmark public text in the study of ageing.
timeline.zh: 出版《老年》，综合历史、文学、经济与日常生活，分析社会如何把老年人塑造成“他者”；它成为老年社会研究的重要公共文本。

timeline.en: Signed the Manifesto of the 343 — 343 women publicly declaring they had had abortions, igniting the French reproductive rights movement.
timeline.zh: 签署《343 人宣言》——343 名女性公开承认自己堕过胎，点燃法国生育权运动。

timeline.en: Backed Gisèle Halimi's association Choisir and lent public weight to the campaign around the 1972 Bobigny abortion trial; that case and the sustained mobilisation together produced the Veil Law of 1975.
timeline.zh: 支持 Gisèle Halimi 建立的“Choisir”协会，并在 1972 年 Bobigny 堕胎案相关运动中发挥公共影响；该案与持续动员共同推动 1975 年《韦伊法》。

timeline.en: Served as president of the League of Women's Rights, and in 1977 co-founded the theoretical journal Questions féministes with Christine Delphy and others.
timeline.zh: 出任法国女性权利同盟主席；1977 年又与 Christine Delphy 等人共同创办理论期刊《Questions féministes》。

timeline.en: Died in Paris at seventy-eight, leaving an archive across genres: novels, philosophy, memoir, letters, editing and political engagement.
timeline.zh: 卒于巴黎，七十八岁。她留下小说、哲学论著、回忆录、书信、编辑工作与政治介入构成的跨体裁档案。

sources.en: On the founding of Les Temps modernes

story.en:
She did not set out to write the book that would change how half the world understood itself. She set out to answer one question: why had she always been told she was 'the second'?

The answer became The Second Sex: one is not born a woman; one becomes one. The sentence landed like a philosophical earthquake.

She was buried with Sartre's name beside hers and Algren's ring on her finger. She never chose just one way to live.
story.zh:
她并非刻意要写一本改变半个世界自我认知的书。她只是想回答一个问题：为什么她总是被告知自己是「第二位」？

答案成了《第二性》：一个人不是生为女人，而是变成女人的。这句话像一场哲学地震。

她下葬时，萨特的名字在她身旁，阿尔格伦的戒指在她指上。她从不只选一种活法。

intro.en: Writing was one link in a long chain of trades: she worked in public transport, sang, danced, wrote plays, edited, coordinated for the civil rights movement, taught and directed. All of it went into seven volumes of autobiography, poetry, screen work and public speech.
intro.zh: 写作只是她漫长职业链的一环：她做过公共交通从业者、歌手、舞者、剧作家、编辑、民权组织协调人、教师与导演。她把这些行业经验带进七卷自传、诗歌、影视和公共演讲。

timeline.en: At sixteen, became San Francisco's first Black woman streetcar conductor.
timeline.zh: 十六岁成为旧金山第一位非裔女性缆车售票员。

timeline.en: Released the album Miss Calypso, having already toured twenty-two countries as a singer and dancer with Porgy and Bess.
timeline.zh: 发行专辑《Miss Calypso》；此前以歌手舞者身份随《波吉与贝丝》巡演二十二国。

timeline.en: Wrote and performed Cabaret for Freedom with Godfrey Cambridge to raise money for the Southern Christian Leadership Conference — she proved herself with that show first.
timeline.zh: 与 Godfrey Cambridge 自编自演歌舞剧《Cabaret for Freedom》为南方基督教领袖会议筹款——她是先靠这场演出证明了自己。

timeline.en: Became Northern Coordinator of the Southern Christian Leadership Conference, working with Martin Luther King Jr.
timeline.zh: 出任南方基督教领袖会议北方协调人，与马丁·路德·金共事。

timeline.en: Edited the Arab Observer in Cairo, then worked at the University of Ghana's School of Music and Drama and wrote for the Ghanaian Times and African Review — a formative pan-African intellectual period.
timeline.zh: 在开罗任《Arab Observer》编辑，后在加纳大学音乐与戏剧学院工作，并为《Ghanaian Times》和《African Review》撰稿，形成一段重要的泛非知识分子经历。

timeline.en: Published I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings, among the first autobiographies by a Black American woman to reach the mainstream bestseller market, and long a fixture of school curricula and literary debate.
timeline.zh: 出版《我知道笼中鸟为何歌唱》，成为第一批进入主流畅销市场的非裔美国女性自传之一，并长期进入学校课程与文学讨论。

timeline.en: Nominated for a Pulitzer for poetry, a Tony for Broadway, and an Emmy for Roots; she later won three Grammys for spoken-word recordings, across poetry, theatre, television and voice.
timeline.zh: 诗集获普利策奖提名、百老汇演出获托尼奖提名、《根》演出获艾美奖提名；她后来又以朗诵录音三获格莱美，横跨诗歌、戏剧、电视与声音表演。

timeline.en: Wrote Georgia, Georgia — the first Black American woman to have her screenplay filmed.
timeline.zh: 编剧《Georgia, Georgia》——第一位剧本被拍成电影的非裔美国女性。

timeline.en: Appointed Reynolds Professor at Wake Forest University, where she taught for more than thirty years.
timeline.zh: 受聘维克森林大学 Reynolds 讲席终身教授，此后任教三十余年。

timeline.en: Recited On the Pulse of Morning at Clinton's inauguration — the first inaugural poem since Frost in 1961, and the first delivered by a Black person or a woman. The recording won a Grammy.
timeline.zh: 在克林顿就职典礼上朗诵《On the Pulse of Morning》——自 1961 年弗罗斯特以来第一首就职诗，她也是第一位担此的黑人与女性。该录音获格莱美奖。

timeline.en: Directed her first feature, Down in the Delta, at seventy. She was not the first Black woman to direct a mainstream feature — Euzhan Palcy and others came earlier — but it was a significant stop in a career spent crossing trades.
timeline.zh: 七十岁完成剧情长片导演处女作《Down in the Delta》。她并非第一位执导主流剧情长片的非裔女性——Euzhan Palcy 等导演更早——但这是她跨行业创作能力的重要一站。

timeline.en: Awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom by President Obama.
timeline.zh: 获奥巴马总统颁授总统自由勋章。

sources.en: Down in the Delta, production record

story.en:
At eight years old she stopped speaking. She believed her voice had killed a man, so she locked it away for five years.

A teacher named Bertha Flowers gave her books of poetry and said: read them aloud. That silence broke open into a voice that would address presidents and fill stadiums.

What felt like a cage turned out to be a kind of preparation.
story.zh:
八岁那年她停止了说话。她相信自己的声音杀了一个人，于是将它锁起来五年。

一位名叫伯莎·弗劳尔斯的老师给她诗集，说：大声读出来。那段沉默裂开了，涌出的声音日后在总统面前回响、让体育场座无虚席。

看似牢笼的东西，原来是一种准备。

intro.en: She ran an independent painting practice in Rome, Florence, Naples and London, entering academies, courts and the market for large religious commissions. She gave women from history movement, force and decision — and her professional achievement should not be eclipsed by the trial.
intro.zh: 她在罗马、佛罗伦萨、那不勒斯和伦敦经营独立画家事业，进入学院、宫廷与大型宗教委托市场。她让女性历史人物拥有动作、力量与决断；职业成就不应被审判经历遮住。

timeline.en: Endured the sibille during the rape trial — thin cords tightened around her fingers — without changing a word of her testimony.
timeline.zh: 在强奸案审判中承受 sibille 拶指刑——细绳勒紧手指——证词一字未改。

timeline.en: She testified repeatedly across a seven-month trial; Tassi was convicted and sentenced to exile, though the sentence was never enforced. The transcript preserves her testimony inside a system stacked against her.
timeline.zh: 她在七个月庭审中反复作证，Tassi 最终被判有罪并处流放；判决实际没有执行。审判记录保存了她在高度不利制度中的证词。

timeline.en: Immediately after the trial she painted the first version of Judith Slaying Holofernes, now in Naples — Judith's arms sinewed and certain, blood arcing across the sheets.
timeline.zh: 审判刚结束，她画下《朱迪斯斩杀荷罗孚尼》第一版（那不勒斯藏）——朱迪斯的手臂有筋腱、有把握，血弧横过床单。

timeline.en: Painted the Allegory of Inclination for the Casa Buonarroti, the Michelangelo family house, hung alongside the leading male painters of Florence.
timeline.zh: 为米开朗基罗家族的 Casa Buonarroti 绘制《倾向的寓言》，与当时佛罗伦萨最顶尖的男画家同列一室。

timeline.en: Became the first woman admitted to the Accademia delle Arti del Disegno in Florence. Membership raised her professional standing and helped her sign contracts, buy materials and handle legal matters independently — though it was not the equivalent of full modern legal personhood.
timeline.zh: 成为佛罗伦萨迪塞诺艺术学院第一位女性成员。会员资格提升了职业信誉，并有助于她独立签订合同、购买材料与处理法律事务；不能把它等同现代完整“法人资格”。

timeline.en: Painted the Uffizi version of Judith Slaying Holofernes — her defining work.
timeline.zh: 绘制《朱迪斯斩杀荷罗孚尼》乌菲齐版——她的代表作。

timeline.en: Ran a workshop in Naples with assistants and took on the altarpiece cycle for Pozzuoli Cathedral; she is among the earliest women known to have won large public religious commissions.
timeline.zh: 在那不勒斯经营画室、雇佣助手，并承接波佐利主教座堂祭坛画组；她是已知很早获得大型公共宗教委托的女画家之一。

timeline.en: The Allegory of Painting is often read as her self-portrait: because Painting is female in the iconographic tradition, she could make the allegory of the profession and the artist the same figure. Whether it is strictly a self-portrait is still discussed.
timeline.zh: 《绘画的寓言》常被解释为她的自画像：因为“绘画”按图像传统是女性形象，她得以把职业寓言与艺术家本人重叠；作品是否严格为自画像仍有讨论。

timeline.en: Went to London and the court of Charles I, rejoining her father Orazio and probably helping complete the Queen's House ceiling at Greenwich; she also made her own work for the royal collection.
timeline.zh: 赴伦敦进入查理一世宫廷，与父亲 Orazio 重聚并可能合作完成格林尼治王后宫天顶画；她也为英国王室收藏创作自己的作品。

timeline.en: Her clients included Cosimo II de' Medici, Philip IV of Spain and Charles I of England, and she corresponded with Galileo. More than thirty surviving letters in her own hand argue price, schedule and unpaid invoices — she ran the business herself.
timeline.zh: 客户名单包括美第奇的科西莫二世、西班牙腓力四世、英王查理一世；与伽利略有书信往来。存世三十余封她亲笔谈价钱、工期与催款的信——她是自己经营生意的。

coda.en: Her last dated activity is from 1654; the year and cause of her death are unknown. The old account of the 1656 Naples plague lacks direct evidence.
coda.zh: 最后有日期的活动记录在 1654 年；确切卒年和死因不明，过去常说死于 1656 年那不勒斯瘟疫，但缺少直接证据。

story.en:
They tortured her fingers to test whether she was lying. She looked at her rapist across the courtroom and said: 'This is the ring you give me, and these are your promises.'

Then she spent forty years painting women who were not victims — Judith with sinew in her arms, Susanna refusing to look away, Cleopatra choosing her own end.

You become undeniable. That is the only strategy that holds.
story.zh:
他们绞紧她的手指来验证她是否在撒谎。她隔着法庭望着施暴者说：「这就是你给我的戒指，这就是你的承诺。」

然后她用四十年画那些不是受害者的女人——双臂有力的朱迪斯，拒绝移开目光的苏珊娜，自己选择结局的克里奥帕特拉。

让自己变得不可否认。这是唯一站得住的策略。

intro.en: More than a record-setting pilot: an aviation editor, author, company executive, clothing entrepreneur and builder of women's flying organisations. She used media, business and a university post to fund flying, and widened both the idea and the opportunity of women in aviation.
intro.zh: 她不只是纪录飞行员，还是航空编辑、作家、企业管理者、服装创业者与女性飞行组织建设者。她用媒体、商业和大学职位为飞行筹资，也扩大女性进入航空业的想象与机会。

timeline.en: Began flight instruction with Neta Snook, paying for lessons by working as a stenographer, photographer and truck driver.
timeline.zh: 跟随 Neta Snook 开始飞行训练，靠速记员、摄影师、卡车司机的工作支付学费。

timeline.en: Set a women's altitude record of 14,000 feet; the following year she became the sixteenth woman in the world to hold an FAI licence. Her career did not begin as a passenger.
timeline.zh: 创下女子飞行高度纪录 14,000 英尺；次年成为全球第十六位取得 FAI 飞行执照的女性。她的职业生涯不是从当乘客开始的。

timeline.en: Became the first woman to cross the Atlantic by air — as a passenger. She insisted she was "just baggage, like a sack of potatoes."
timeline.zh: 成为第一位飞越大西洋的女性——以乘客身份。她坚持说自己「只是行李，像一袋土豆」。

timeline.en: Aviation editor at Cosmopolitan for two years, using the column to recruit women into flying, and published the bestseller 20 Hrs., 40 Min. in the same period.
timeline.zh: 任《Cosmopolitan》航空编辑两年，把专栏当成向女性招募飞行员的阵地；同期出版畅销书《20 Hrs., 40 Min.》。

timeline.en: Co-founded the Ninety-Nines in November with ninety-nine charter members, and became its first president in 1931.
timeline.zh: 11 月共同创办「九九会」（99 位创始女飞行员），1931 年出任首任会长。

timeline.en: Became vice-president of the Ludington Line, the first regional shuttle between New York and Washington. She had started building the industry itself.
timeline.zh: 出任 Ludington Line 副总裁——纽约–华盛顿首条区域穿梭航线。她开始建造这个行业本身。

timeline.en: Set an autogyro altitude record of 18,415 feet — she was test-flying rotorcraft too.
timeline.zh: 创下自转旋翼机高度纪录 18,415 英尺——她也在试飞旋翼机。

timeline.en: Flew the Atlantic solo in 14 hours 56 minutes, the first woman to do it. Congress awarded her the Distinguished Flying Cross, the first woman to receive it.
timeline.zh: 以 14 小时 56 分单人飞越大西洋，第一位做到的女性。国会授予杰出飞行十字勋章，她是第一位获此勋章的女性。

timeline.en: Became the first woman to fly solo non-stop across the United States.
timeline.zh: 成为第一位不着陆单人横越美国东西岸的女性。

timeline.en: Launched a functional clothing line under her own name — washable, easy to move in, made for working women — sold at Macy's and elsewhere. The claim that it was made chiefly from parachute silk is unsupported.
timeline.zh: 推出以自己命名的功能性女装系列，强调可清洗、便于活动与适合职业女性，在梅西等百货销售；“以降落伞绸为主要材料”缺少可靠依据。

timeline.en: Became vice-president of Boston-Maine Airways and National Airways.
timeline.zh: 出任 Boston-Maine Airways 与 National Airways 副总裁。

timeline.en: Became the first person of any sex to fly solo from Hawaii to California.
timeline.zh: 成为第一个从夏威夷单人飞抵加州的人——不分性别。

timeline.en: Career counsellor for women at Purdue, where she pushed the university to fund the Lockheed Electra "flying laboratory"; she was also a member of the National Woman's Party and an early public backer of the Equal Rights Amendment.
timeline.zh: 任普渡大学女性职业顾问，推动普渡设立研究基金买下那架 Lockheed Electra「飞行实验室」；她也是全国妇女党成员与《平等权利修正案》的早期公开支持者。

timeline.en: Departed on a round-the-world flight of 29,000 miles. Her last radio transmission came on 2 July over the Pacific. She was never found.
timeline.zh: 启程环球飞行，全程两万九千英里。7 月 2 日于太平洋上空发出最后一次无线电通讯。她再未被找到。

sources.en: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum
sources.zh: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum

story.en:
The first time she crossed the Atlantic, she was a passenger. She said so plainly: 'I was just baggage, like a sack of potatoes.' Four years later she flew it alone — ice on the wings, flames from the exhaust, a broken altimeter — in fourteen hours and fifty-six minutes.

The airplane does not know your name or your sex. It only knows whether you understand the physics and respect the weather.

She found that a reasonably good argument for equality at altitude.
story.zh:
第一次飞越大西洋时，她是乘客。她直说了：「我只是货物，像一袋土豆。」四年后她独自飞了过去——机翼结冰、排气管喷火、高度计坏了——十四小时五十六分钟。

飞机不知道你的名字或性别。它只知道你是否懂物理、是否敬畏天气。

她觉得这在高空是一个相当有力的平等论据。

intro.en: She built women's climbing organisations, ran her own expeditions, became the first woman to summit Everest in 1975 and the first to complete the Seven Summits in 1992. Then she turned that standing into research on mountain waste, environmental organisations and expeditions for young people.
intro.zh: 她创建女性登山组织、组织海外远征，1975 年成为第一位登顶珠峰的女性，1992 年又成为第一位完成七大洲最高峰的女性。此后她把登山声誉转化为山地垃圾研究、环境组织与青少年登山项目。

timeline.en: Founded the Ladies Climbing Club — Japan's first women's mountaineering organisation — after male climbers refused to climb with her.
timeline.zh: 创办女子登攀俱乐部——日本第一个女性登山组织，起因是男性登山者拒绝与她同行。

timeline.en: As deputy leader of a Japanese women's team, made the second ascent of Annapurna III by a new southern route, and the first by women; the peak had first been climbed in 1961.
timeline.zh: 担任日本女子队副队长，沿南侧新路线完成安纳普尔纳 III 峰第二次登顶、也是首次女性登顶；该峰首登早在 1961 年完成。

timeline.en: Organised and co-led the Japanese Women's Everest Expedition, teaching piano and tutoring to raise the money. She assembled that team herself.
timeline.zh: 组织并副领导日本女子珠峰远征队，为凑经费去教钢琴、当家教。这支队伍是她自己攒出来的。

timeline.en: As deputy leader and climbing leader of the expedition she was buried by an avalanche at Camp II, dug out, and twelve days later became the first woman to stand on the summit of Everest.
timeline.zh: 作为日本女子珠峰队副队长兼登攀队长，在二号营地遭雪崩掩埋、获救后继续攀登，十二天后成为第一位登顶珠峰的女性。

timeline.en: Completed the Seven Summits, the highest peak on each continent — the first woman to do so.
timeline.zh: 完成七大洲最高峰，第一位达成的女性。

timeline.en: Represented the Himalayan Adventure Trust of Japan from its founding in 1990, working on mountain conservation; in 2000 she completed a master's at Kyushu University with a thesis on waste left by Everest expeditions — not a general environmental science degree.
timeline.zh: 1990 年日本喜马拉雅探险信托成立，她任代表并推动山地环境保护；2000 年完成九州大学比较社会文化研究科硕士，论文研究珠峰登山垃圾，而非笼统“环境科学学位”。

timeline.en: Led schoolchildren from the areas struck by the 2011 earthquake and tsunami up Mount Fuji, year after year, having climbed the highest peak in more than seventy countries.
timeline.zh: 年年带东日本大地震灾区的中学生登富士山，一生登顶七十多个国家的最高峰。

timeline.en: Diagnosed with stomach cancer, she kept leading youth expeditions until months before her death.
timeline.zh: 确诊胃癌，直到去世前几个月仍在带青少年远征。

coda.en: She died on 20 October 2016. An asteroid and a mountain range on Pluto now carry her name.
coda.zh: 2016 年 10 月 20 日去世。一颗小行星与冥王星上的一列山脉以她命名。

story.en:
She was a frail child in Fukushima. Male climbers refused to climb with her. She founded her own club, sewed waterproof gloves from car covers, and took her team to Everest.

At 6,300 metres an avalanche buried her. The Sherpas dug her out. She kept going.

I did not intend to be the first woman on Everest, she said. I prefer to remember that I was the thirty-sixth person. The mountain does not count differently.
story.zh:
她是福岛的一个体弱的孩子。男性登山者拒绝与她同行。她自己建了俱乐部，用汽车罩布缝防水手套，带着队伍去了珠峰。

在六千三百米处雪崩将她掩埋。夏尔巴向导把她挖了出来。她继续攀登。

我并非有意成为第一位登上珠峰的女性，她说。我更愿意记得我是第三十六个人。山不会用不同的方式计数。

era.zh: 维多利亚时代 · 英国

intro.en: She joined battlefield nursing, hospital management, statistical analysis and administrative reform into one practice. The fall in deaths at Scutari came from better nursing, changed supply and the Sanitary Commission's work on the building together; afterwards she used data to make preventable disease a problem the army and government had to answer for.
intro.zh: 她把战地护理、医院管理、统计分析和行政改革连在一起。斯库塔里的死亡下降发生在护理改进、补给变化与卫生委员会整治环境的共同作用下；她随后用数据把可预防疾病变成军队与政府必须处理的制度问题。

timeline.en: Arrived at Scutari with thirty-eight nurses during the Crimean War and found soldiers dying of cholera and typhus at a rate of 42%.
timeline.zh: 克里米亚战争期间带三十八名护士抵达斯库塔里，发现士兵死于霍乱与斑疹伤寒，死亡率高达 42%。

timeline.en: Deaths fell sharply after the Sanitary Commission cleared the sewers and improved ventilation and water in 1855. Reanalysing the data at home, she came to identify crowding, sewage and poor ventilation as the central causes; "she publicly admitted she had been completely wrong" is an over-dramatised summary.
timeline.zh: 卫生委员会 1855 年疏通下水道、改善通风和供水后死亡率显著下降。她回国后重新分析数据，越来越明确地把拥挤、污水与通风不良列为核心原因；“她公开承认自己完全错了”是过度戏剧化的概括。

timeline.en: Pushed for the Royal Commission on the Health of the Army and wrote its 830-page report. The entire British military medical system was rebuilt from it.
timeline.zh: 推动成立英国陆军卫生问题皇家委员会，撰写 830 页报告。整个英军医疗体系是照她的报告重建的。

timeline.en: Designed and popularised the polar area diagram — the "Nightingale rose" — showing at a glance that preventable disease killed far more men than wounds; she was not its sole inventor. The same year she became the first woman elected to the Statistical Society of London.
timeline.zh: 设计并推广极坐标面积图（“南丁格尔玫瑰”），直观显示可预防疾病远比战伤致命；她不是极坐标图的唯一发明人。同年成为伦敦统计学会第一位女性会员。

timeline.en: Proposed standardised hospital statistical forms to the International Statistical Congress, aiming to unify how disease, recovery and death were classified so hospitals could be compared — an important early attempt at measuring quality of care.
timeline.zh: 为国际统计大会提出标准化医院统计表格，希望统一疾病、康复与死亡分类，使医院之间的数据能够比较；这是医疗质量测量的重要早期尝试。

timeline.en: Published Notes on Nursing for households and ordinary carers, explaining ventilation, cleanliness, diet and how to observe a patient; it became one of the most influential public guides to modern nursing.
timeline.zh: 出版《护理札记》，面向家庭与普通照护者解释通风、清洁、饮食与观察病情；它成为最有影响力的现代护理公共指南之一。

timeline.en: Spent decades on public health in India, supplying evidence and analysis to the royal commission on the Indian army and lobbying for water, drainage and rural sanitation. She shaped the commission without ever chairing it.
timeline.zh: 此后数十年研究印度公共卫生，为印度陆军卫生皇家委员会提供证据和分析，并持续游说供水、排水与乡村卫生改革；她影响委员会，但并未担任其主席。

timeline.en: Founded the Nightingale Training School at St Thomas' Hospital, professionalising nursing through systematic training, discipline and hospital practice. Calling it "the world's first secular nursing school" depends on how the terms are defined.
timeline.zh: 在圣托马斯医院创办南丁格尔护士训练学校，以系统训练、纪律与医院实践推动护理职业化。把它称为“世界第一所世俗护理学校”存在定义争议。

timeline.en: Published Notes on Hospitals, setting out the "Nightingale ward" — ventilation, spacing between beds, daylight — and hospitals were built to it worldwide for the next half century.
timeline.zh: 出版《Notes on Hospitals》，确立「南丁格尔式病房」的设计规范（通风、床距、采光），此后半个世纪全球医院照此建造。

timeline.en: Appointed to the Order of Merit by Edward VII, the first woman ever to receive it. She wrote some two hundred books and reports and fourteen thousand letters, most of it during the forty years she spent largely bedridden.
timeline.zh: 获爱德华七世授予功绩勋章——史上第一位获此荣誉的女性。她一生写下约两百部著作报告与一万四千封信，其中大部分完成于卧床的四十年间。

story.en:
At Scutari she found soldiers dying in rooms without drainage, on floors without linen, treated by men without soap. She did not weep. She counted.

She reduced the death rate from forty-two percent to two. Then she spent forty years bedridden — and from that bed she invented the statistical diagram, founded the first nursing school, and became the first woman appointed to the Order of Merit.

Statistics are not abstractions. They are human lives rendered legible.
story.zh:
在斯库台里她看到士兵在没有排水的房间里、没有床单的地板上、被没有肥皂的人治疗着死去。她没有哭泣。她开始计数。

她将死亡率从百分之四十二降到百分之二。然后她卧床四十年——从那张床上她发明了统计图表、创办了第一所护理学校、成为第一位获授功绩勋章的女性。

统计数字不是抽象概念。它们是被变得可读的人命。

intro.en: She ran a school, worked as a governess, translated, reviewed, wrote novels and political polemic, and became one of the first women in Britain to live mainly by her pen. She put education, economic independence and political rights inside a single argument for women's equality.
intro.zh: 她办学校、做家庭教师、翻译、评论、写小说与政治论战，并成为英国最早主要依靠写作谋生的女性之一。她把教育、经济独立与政治权利放进同一套女性平等论证。

timeline.en: Opened a school for girls at Newington Green with her sister and her friend Fanny Blood — everything she later argued about education came from having actually run a school and actually taught.
timeline.zh: 与妹妹和好友 Fanny Blood 在 Newington Green 创办女子学校——她所有教育主张的来源是她真的办过学校、真的教过。

timeline.en: Published her first book, Thoughts on the Education of Daughters, arguing that women should be raised to reason rather than to ornament.
timeline.zh: 出版第一本书《女儿教育之思考》，主张女性应被养成会推理的人，而非装饰品。

timeline.en: Became a staff writer and translator (from German and French) for Joseph Johnson's Analytical Review, one of the first women in Britain to live entirely by writing — "the first of a new genus," as she put it. The same year, Original Stories from Real Life appeared with illustrations by William Blake.
timeline.zh: 成为 Joseph Johnson《Analytical Review》的专职撰稿人与翻译（译德、法文），是英国最早完全靠写作为生的女性之一——她自称「一个新品种的第一个」。同年《Original Stories from Real Life》由威廉·布莱克配插图。

timeline.en: Published A Vindication of the Rights of Men, among the first and generally the earliest printed reply to Burke's Reflections on the Revolution in France, putting rank and hereditary privilege at the centre of public argument.
timeline.zh: 出版《为人权辩护》，成为对柏克《法国革命论》的第一批、通常被认为最早印行的回应之一，并把等级与世袭特权置于公开论战中心。

timeline.en: Published A Vindication of the Rights of Woman: women appear inferior only because they are denied education. It was reprinted within the year and quickly translated into French and German — not a book rediscovered later, but one with international reach on arrival.
timeline.zh: 出版《女权辩护》：女性显得低等，只因为她们被剥夺了教育。出版当年即再版，并很快译成法文与德文——它不是被后世追认的书，它当场就有国际影响力。

timeline.en: Went to Paris to observe the Revolution, recording political change through the Terror and the war between Britain and France; that eyewitness period became the material for her next book.
timeline.zh: 赴巴黎观察法国大革命，在恐怖统治与英法战争期间持续记录政治变化；这段现场经验成为她下一部历史著作的材料。

timeline.en: Published An Historical and Moral View of the French Revolution — contemporary history written first-hand, in Paris, during the Terror.
timeline.zh: 出版《法国革命的历史与道德观》——她人在巴黎、身处恐怖统治期间写下的第一手当代史。

timeline.en: Travelled through Scandinavia investigating a commercial dispute and turned the politics, trade, landscape and personal observation of the journey into Letters Written in Sweden, Norway and Denmark, a key work of early Romantic travel writing.
timeline.zh: 赴斯堪的纳维亚调查一项商业纠纷，并把沿途政治、贸易、自然与个人观察写成《瑞典、挪威与丹麦书简》，成为早期浪漫主义旅行写作的重要作品。

timeline.en: Wrote the unfinished novel Maria: or, The Wrongs of Woman, bringing marriage law, property rights, confinement and women's desire into one narrative; not the first novel on those subjects, but a radical joining of institutional critique to the form.
timeline.zh: 创作未完成小说《玛丽亚：或女性受害记》，把婚姻法、财产权、监禁与女性欲望写入同一叙事；它不是相关主题的“第一部小说”，但激进地连接了制度批判与小说形式。

timeline.en: Died of an infection following childbirth at thirty-eight; Godwin edited and published Maria and her other unfinished work in 1798.
timeline.zh: 因分娩后的感染去世，终年三十八岁；《玛丽亚》等未完成作品由 William Godwin 于 1798 年整理出版。

sources.zh: 美国国会图书馆原版书目

story.en:
As a teenager she slept outside her mother's bedroom door to shield her from a father who came home drunk and violent. She left home at nineteen. She taught, she nursed, she wrote.

In 1792 she published A Vindication of the Rights of Woman — the argument that women are not naturally inferior, only denied the chance to prove otherwise. It was the first time anyone had said it this clearly.

She died at thirty-eight, eleven days after giving birth to the daughter who would write Frankenstein. The truth does not become less true for being inconvenient to say aloud.
story.zh:
少女时代她睡在母亲卧室门外，替她挡住醉酒施暴的父亲。十九岁离家。她教书、护理、写作。

1792年她出版了《为女权辩护》——论证女性并非天生低劣，只是被剥夺了证明自己的机会。这是有史以来第一次有人把这件事说得如此清楚。

她在三十八岁去世，女儿出生十一天后。真话不会因为说出来不方便就变得不真实。

intro.en: Republican China's lawyer regulations admitted only men. She took a doctorate in law in Paris and in 1926 opened a Shanghai practice on the strength of her French degree, the first recorded Chinese woman lawyer; in 1927 she held judicial office, among the earliest Chinese women to do so, and in 1928 she became one of the first two women in the Legislative Yuan. In 1929 she sat as the only woman on the five-member committee that drafted the Civil Code, and the reports for its first three books carry her name.
intro.zh: 民国律师章程只收男子。她在巴黎取得法学博士，1926 年凭法国学位在上海开业，成为有记载的第一位中国女律师；1927 年出任法院院长，是最早担任司法职务的中国女性之一；1928 年成为立法院最早的两位女委员之一。1929 年她是五人民法起草委员会中唯一的女性，民法前三编的起草报告上有她的名字。

timeline.en: Born on 20 March in Xin'an county, Guangdong. As a child she refused to have her feet bound; at about thirteen she wrote to end the betrothal her grandmother had arranged.
timeline.zh: 3 月 20 日生于广东新安县。幼年拒绝缠足；十三岁左右写信退掉祖母订下的婚约。

timeline.en: By her own account she carried explosives from Tianjin to Beijing for the Tongmenghui's assassination squad in the plots against Yuan Shikai and the general Liangbi. In 1912 she entered Li Shizeng's preparatory school for study in France, and by spring 1914 she was in Paris as Soumay Tcheng, learning French and enrolled in law at the Sorbonne.
timeline.zh: 据她本人记述，为同盟会京津暗杀部把炸药从天津带进北京，参与刺袁世凯、炸良弼的行动。1912 年入李石曾创办的留法预备学校；1914 年春已在巴黎，取西名 Soumay Tcheng，先学法文，再入索邦大学攻读法律。

timeline.en: Attaché to the Chinese delegation at the Paris Peace Conference, handling liaison and the press, and a leading voice among Chinese students opposing the Shandong settlement. On the night of 27–28 June, by her own account, she led students to the chief delegate's lodging and levelled a rosebush branch as a pistol, the night before the delegation declined to sign the Treaty of Versailles.
timeline.zh: 任巴黎和会中国代表团随员，负责联络与新闻，也是留法学生反对山东权益转交日本的带头人之一。6 月 27 日夜，据她自述，她率学生赶到首席代表寓所，折下一根玫瑰枝充作手枪；次日代表团拒签《凡尔赛和约》。

timeline.en: Earned a doctorate in law at the University of Paris; her thesis, Le mouvement constitutionnel en Chine, was published by Sirey in 1925, though some records date the degree 1924.
timeline.zh: 获巴黎大学法学博士；论文《中国的立宪运动》1925 年由 Sirey 出版，也有记载把学位年份记作 1924 年。

timeline.en: Opened a law office in Shanghai's French Concession with fellow Paris graduate Wei Daoming. Chinese lawyer regulations admitted only men, so she put her French law degree before the concession's Mixed Court and won leave to plead there, the first recorded Chinese woman to practise as a lawyer.
timeline.zh: 与留法同学魏道明在上海法租界合开律师事务所。民国律师章程只许男子执业，她便凭法国法学学位向法租界会审公廨申请出庭资格并获准，成为有记载的第一位中国女律师。

timeline.en: Appointed president of the International Settlement's Provisional Court, but the sitting president refused to leave and she never sat; she then presided over the Second Special Court in the French Concession, among the earliest Chinese women in judicial office.
timeline.zh: 获任上海公共租界临时法院院长，因原院长拒不让位而未能到任；随后出任法租界第二特区法院院长，是最早担任司法职务的中国女性之一。

timeline.en: Named to the new Legislative Yuan in November, one of its first two women, by appointment rather than election.
timeline.zh: 11 月获任新成立的立法院委员，是最早的两位女委员之一；此时为任命，而非后来的民选。

timeline.en: Appointed on 29 January as one of five legislators, and the only woman, to draft the Civil Code; the committee's reports for the General Principles, Obligations and Property books, 967 articles promulgated within the year, carry her name alongside the others'.
timeline.zh: 1 月 29 日入选五人民法起草委员会，是其中唯一的女性；总则、债、物权三编共 967 条于年内公布，起草报告由她与其他委员共同署名。

timeline.en: Stepped down from the drafting committee after the property book, remaining in the Legislative Yuan as it completed without her the family and succession books (promulgated 26 December) that gave daughters equal inheritance, made engagement the couple's own act (Art. 972) and allowed divorce by consent or by court on stated grounds.
timeline.zh: 物权编完成后她辞去起草委员职务，留在立法院；此后完成的亲属、继承两编（12 月 26 日公布）确立女儿平等继承，婚约由男女当事人自行订定（第 972 条），离婚则可两愿或经法院裁判。

timeline.en: Left the Legislative Yuan to practise again in Shanghai and headed the Shanghai College of Law and Politics through the 1930s (sources differ on the exact dates). Impeached in 1932 over court funds from her 1927 post, she stood trial in 1933; withdrawal of the prosecution was reported in 1935.
timeline.zh: 离开立法院回上海重操律师业，并在 1930 年代出任上海法政学院院长（任职起止年份各家记载不一）。1932 年因 1927 年法院任内款项遭弹劾，1933 年出庭受审，1935 年传出撤销起诉。

timeline.en: After the Japanese attack on Shanghai she organised civilian relief in the International Settlement, then moved to wartime Chongqing.
timeline.zh: 日军进攻上海后，她在公共租界组织平民救济，随后转赴战时陪都重庆。
