timeline.en: Published My Revolutionary Years in New York while raising funds for United China Relief and other wartime relief in the United States.
timeline.zh: 在美国为联合援华会募款、从事战时救济期间，于纽约出版自传《我的革命岁月》。

timeline.en: Elected to the first constitutional Legislative Yuan from Shanghai.
timeline.zh: 在行宪后第一届立法委员选举中当选上海选区立法委员。

timeline.en: Died of cancer in Los Angeles on 16 December, aged 68.
timeline.zh: 12 月 16 日因癌症在洛杉矶去世，享年 68 岁。

coda.en: Article 972 of the 1930 Civil Code, passed by the Legislative Yuan she sat in — an engagement 'shall be made by the man and woman themselves' — still stands in Taiwan's Civil Code in its original wording.
coda.zh: 她所在的立法院通过的 1930 年民法第 972 条「婚约，应由男女当事人自行订定」，至今仍以原文保留在台湾现行民法中。

sources.zh: 民国人物传记辞典 X-Boorman

sources.en: Sun Xiaoxia on the Civil Code drafters (aisixiang)
sources.zh: 孙笑侠《民事立法宗师：史尚宽生平考略》

sources.en: Civil Code as promulgated 26 Dec 1930 (Taipei legal database)
sources.zh: 台北市法规数据库 · 1930 年民法历史版本

story.en:
Republican China's bar admitted only men. She went round it: a Paris doctorate in law, then in 1926 a Shanghai office, her French degree winning her leave to plead.

Court president in 1927, one of the first two women in the Legislative Yuan in 1928, the only woman on the Civil Code committee in 1929: the reports for its first three books carry her name; the 1930 family and succession books were finished after she left.

'A revolutionary by nature,' she called herself; the law was where she put it.
story.zh:
民国的律师章程只收男子。她绕了过去：先在巴黎拿到法学博士，1926 年在上海开业，凭法国学位取得法租界法院的出庭资格。

1927 年出任法院院长，1928 年成为立法院最早的两位女委员之一，1929 年是五人民法起草委员会里唯一的女性：民法前三编的起草报告上有她的名字；1930 年的亲属、继承两编，则完成于她离开委员会之后。

她自称「生来就是革命者」，而法律是她安放这股性子的地方。

intro.en: A butcher's daughter from Montauban who taught herself in the salons of Paris, she fought the Comédie-Française for five years to stage an anti-slavery play, petitioned the Assembly for public works, relief for widows and the right to divorce, and in September 1791 rewrote the Declaration of the Rights of Man article by article with a woman in it. Her Declaration never became law; its force was to hold the Revolution to its own words. She was guillotined in November 1793 for a poster proposing that citizens vote on their form of government.
intro.zh: 蒙托邦屠户之女，在巴黎的沙龙里自学成才。她为一部反奴隶制剧本与法兰西喜剧院缠斗五年，终于把它推上舞台；向议会提出公共工程、寡妇救济、离婚权等方案；1791 年 9 月，她把《人权宣言》逐条改写，让女人写进每一条。这份宣言从未成为法律，它的力量在于逼革命兑现自己的承诺。1793 年 11 月，她因一张主张由公民投票决定政体的海报被送上断头台。

timeline.en: Widowed at eighteen, she left Montauban for Paris with her small son, renamed herself Olympe de Gouges, and set about her own education in the capital's salons and theatres.
timeline.zh: 十八岁守寡后，她带着幼子离开蒙托邦来到巴黎，给自己取名奥兰普·德古热，在首都的沙龙与剧院里自修补课。

timeline.en: She submitted Zamore et Mirza, a play against colonial slavery, anonymously to the Comédie-Française; the troupe read it on 28 June with mockery and shelved it once her name was known. In September a lettre de cachet threatening her with the Bastille was drawn up over a line in her letters to the actors. She refused to withdraw the play.
timeline.zh: 她将反殖民奴隶制的剧本《扎莫尔与米尔扎》匿名投给法兰西喜剧院；6 月 28 日剧团一边讥笑一边宣读，得知作者是她之后便束之高阁。9 月，因她写给演员的信里一句话，一封以巴士底狱相威胁的密札被拟就。她拒绝撤稿。

timeline.en: She printed her collected works, attached the essay Réflexions sur les hommes nègres to the play, published a plan for a voluntary patriotic tax in the Journal général de France, and had the Comédie-Française summoned before the Châtelet court.
timeline.zh: 她自费刊印文集，把《关于黑人的思考》一文附在剧本之后，在《法兰西总报》发表自愿爱国税方案，并把法兰西喜剧院告上沙特莱法庭。

timeline.en: She put proposals before the public and the National Assembly: state-funded public works and employment, relief for widows and orphans, civil rights for children born outside marriage, the right to divorce, an end to the death penalty. They remained proposals; the divorce law of September 1792 passed without any clear trace of her hand.
timeline.zh: 她向公众与国民议会提出一系列方案：由国家出资的公共工程与就业、对寡妇孤儿的救济、非婚生子女的民事权利、离婚权、废除死刑。这些始终只是方案；1792 年 9 月离婚法通过，也看不出与她有直接关联。

timeline.en: She saw her play open at last as L'Esclavage des Noirs at the Théâtre de la Nation before about a thousand spectators, hissed and applauded by turns. She lost it after three performances, when colonists and slave-trade merchants who rented boxes by the year threatened to cancel them.
timeline.zh: 她终于看到剧本以《黑人的奴役》为名在国家剧院首演，约千名观众嘘声与掌声交替。演到第三场，按年包厢的殖民者与奴隶贸易商威胁退订，她失去了舞台。

timeline.en: She staged Le Couvent, ou les Vœux forcés, on women forced into convents by their families — her greatest success in the theatre.
timeline.zh: 她推出《修道院，或被迫的誓愿》，写女性被家人逼入修道院——这是她在剧场里最成功的一部戏。

timeline.en: She published the Déclaration des droits de la femme et de la citoyenne: seventeen articles mirroring the 1789 Declaration, addressed to the Queen, opening 'Man, are you capable of being just?' and closing with a model marriage contract between equals. Article X: woman has the right to mount the scaffold; she must equally have the right to mount the rostrum.
timeline.zh: 她发表《女权与女公民权宣言》：十七条逐条对应 1789 年的《人权宣言》，题献给王后，开篇便问「男人，你能做到公正吗？」，末尾附一份男女平等的婚约范本。第十条：女人既有走上断头台的权利，就同样应有登上讲坛的权利。

timeline.en: She published the definitive L'Esclavage des Noirs with a preface answering the charge that it was incendiary, wrote against revolutionary violence from the summer on, and on 16 December offered the Convention to help defend Louis XVI — out of her opposition to the death penalty and her own constitutional convictions alike.
timeline.zh: 她出版《黑人的奴役》定本，在序言里回应「煽动」之责；自夏天起公开反对革命暴力；12 月 16 日致函国民公会，请求参与路易十六的辩护——既出于反对死刑，也出于她自己的宪政主张。

timeline.en: She composed a poster, Les Trois Urnes, proposing that primary assemblies vote among a single republic, a federal republic and a monarchy to avert civil war. The bill-poster refused to put it up.
timeline.zh: 她写下海报《三只票箱》，主张由基层公民大会在单一共和、联邦共和与君主制之间投票，以避免内战。张贴工拒绝上墙。

timeline.en: She was arrested over the poster and held for more than three months.
timeline.zh: 她因这张海报被捕，羁押三个多月。

timeline.en: Before the Revolutionary Tribunal, with no defender, she argued her own case: she had wanted only to prevent civil war. The indictment cited Les Trois Urnes and other 1793 writings, not the Declaration. Convicted, she declared herself pregnant; the health officers did not confirm it.
timeline.zh: 在革命法庭上，她没有辩护人，只能自辩：她只想避免内战。起诉书列举的是《三只票箱》等 1793 年的文字，而非那份宣言。判决后她宣称自己怀孕，医官未予认定。

timeline.en: She was guillotined on the Place de la Révolution, aged forty-five, reportedly saying: 'Children of the Fatherland, you will avenge my death.' Two weeks later Chaumette held her up to Parisian women as 'that virago, the woman-man'.
timeline.zh: 她在革命广场被处决，终年四十五岁，据传留下一句：「祖国的孩子们，你们会为我的死复仇。」两周后，肖梅特在巴黎妇女面前拿她作反面教材，称她「泼妇、男人婆」。

coda.en: Her Declaration was barely noticed in her lifetime. Olivier Blanc's 1981 biography and Benoîte Groult's 1986 edition brought it back; in 2016 the Assemblée nationale placed her marble bust in its Salle des Quatre-Colonnes.
coda.zh: 她的宣言生前几乎无人在意。1981 年奥利维耶·布朗的传记与 1986 年伯努瓦特·格鲁的编本让它重回视野；2016 年，法国国民议会在四柱厅立起她的大理石半身像。

sources.en: Les Droits de la femme (1791 text, Wikisource)

sources.zh: 审判记录英译，乔治梅森大学

story.en:
The Comédie-Française shelved her anti-slavery play for five years under colonial pressure. She printed her works, sued the theatre, and on 28 December 1789 saw it staged — for three nights.

Plays, petitions for public works and divorce, then in September 1791 seventeen articles answering the men's Declaration of 1789: never law, but a demand that the Revolution keep its own word.

'Woman has the right to mount the scaffold; she must equally have the right to mount the rostrum.' In November 1793 the Republic granted her only the first.
story.zh:
法兰西喜剧院在殖民者施压下把她的反奴隶制剧本压了五年。她刊印文集、把剧院告上法庭，1789 年 12 月 28 日终于看它上演——只演了三场。

戏剧、关于公共工程与离婚权的方案，再到 1791 年 9 月回应《人权宣言》的十七条——它从未成为法律，却逼革命兑现自己的承诺。

「女人既有走上断头台的权利，就同样应有登上讲坛的权利。」1793 年 11 月，共和国只给了她前一种。

intro.en: Raised in a Cairo harem and married at thirteen, Huda Sha'arawi helped organise the women's street demonstrations of the 1919 revolution, founded the Egyptian Feminist Union in 1923 and led it for twenty-four years. She tied Egypt's independence to women's education and citizenship: she pressed for girls' schooling and marriage-law reform, published journals in French and Arabic, and in 1944 convened the congress from which a pan-Arab women's union grew.
intro.zh: 胡达·沙拉维在开罗深闺长大，十三岁被嫁人。1919 年革命中她参与组织妇女上街示威，1923 年创立埃及女性联盟并领导了二十四年。她把埃及独立与女性教育、公民权利联系在一起：推动女孩入学和婚姻法改革，出版法文与阿拉伯文刊物，并在 1944 年召集大会，泛阿拉伯妇女联盟由此而生。

timeline.en: Married at thirteen to a cousin in his forties, she separated from him after fifteen months when he broke his written monogamy pledge, and spent the next seven years studying on her own terms.
timeline.zh: 十三岁被嫁给四十多岁的表亲；十五个月后对方违背书面的一夫一妻承诺，她随即分居，用之后七年按自己的意愿读书。

timeline.en: Helped found Mubarrat Muhammad Ali, a women's charity running a dispensary for poor women and children, and arranged public lectures for women at the Egyptian University; in 1914 she helped found the Intellectual Association of Egyptian Women.
timeline.zh: 参与创办穆罕默德·阿里慈善会，为贫苦妇女儿童开设诊所，并在埃及大学安排面向女性的公开讲座；1914 年又参与建立埃及妇女知识协会。

timeline.en: On 16 March she helped organise the first women's street demonstration of the revolution: some 300 veiled women marched through Cairo against the British, stood three hours under British rifles and did not disperse.
timeline.zh: 3 月 16 日，她参与组织了革命中第一次妇女街头示威：约三百名蒙面纱的妇女穿过开罗抗议英国统治，在英军枪口下站了三个小时，没有散去。

timeline.en: Elected first president of the Wafdist Women's Central Committee, the first political organisation of Egyptian women, she gave women's nationalist organising a lasting base; in 1922 she chaired the mass meeting that launched a women's boycott of British goods.
timeline.zh: 当选华夫脱妇女中央委员会首任主席——这是埃及妇女的第一个政治组织，使妇女的民族独立运动有了持续运作的组织基础；1922 年她主持大会，发起妇女抵制英国货运动。

timeline.en: On 16 March she founded the Egyptian Feminist Union at her Cairo home and led it until her death, demanding schools for girls, a higher marriage age, curbs on polygamy and divorce, political participation and the vote. She counted among its first gains a rule, won that year alongside other reformers, that barred the registration of marriages for girls under 16.
timeline.zh: 3 月 16 日，她在开罗家中创立埃及女性联盟并领导至去世，要求女孩入学、提高婚龄、限制一夫多妻和任意休妻，并争取政治参与和选举权。同年与其他改革者一道争得的一条规则——未满十六岁的女孩不得登记结婚——被她视为联盟最早的收获之一。

timeline.en: Returning from the International Woman Suffrage Alliance congress in Rome, she and Saiza Nabarawi stepped off the train at Cairo station and drew back the veils from their faces — the face veil, not the head covering — while the women on the platform applauded.
timeline.zh: 从罗马的国际妇女选举权同盟大会归来，她与赛扎·纳巴拉维在开罗车站走下火车，掀开脸上的面纱——是面纱，不是头巾——站台上的妇女鼓掌。

timeline.en: Led women pickets at the opening of the new parliament and submitted 32 nationalist and feminist demands; the government ignored them, and over that exclusion and wider disagreements about nationalist politics she resigned from the Wafdist committee and carried on through the independent Union.
timeline.zh: 率领妇女在新议会开幕时纠察示威，递交三十二项民族与女权诉求；政府置之不理，她因女性被排除在外以及民族政治路线上的分歧辞去华夫脱委员会职务，转而以独立的女性联盟为阵地继续。

timeline.en: Launched L'Égyptienne, a French-language monthly edited by Nabarawi that ran until 1940 and gave women's political arguments a platform, and opened the Union's club for women; she added an Arabic sister journal, al-Misriyya, in 1937.
timeline.zh: 创办法文月刊《埃及女性》，由纳巴拉维主编，一直出版到 1940 年，为女性的政治主张建立了发表阵地；同时开设联盟的妇女俱乐部。1937 年她又推出阿拉伯文姊妹刊《埃及女人》。

timeline.en: Carried the Union's bills restricting polygamy and verbal divorce as far as the cabinet, which approved them, and lost them to King Fuad's rejection; she kept pressing for girls' secondary schools, and in 1928 saw the first women enter the Egyptian University.
timeline.zh: 把联盟限制一夫多妻和口头休妻的法案推进到内阁并获通过，却败于国王福阿德的否决；她继续推动女子中学，1928 年看到第一批女生进入埃及大学。

timeline.en: Named a vice-president of the International Alliance of Women at its Istanbul congress, keeping the Egyptian movement inside the international one.
timeline.zh: 在伊斯坦布尔大会上被推举为国际妇女同盟副主席，让埃及的运动始终立于国际运动之中。

timeline.en: Convened in Cairo in October a regional women's conference on the question of Palestine, carrying the Union's work beyond Egypt's borders.
timeline.zh: 10 月在开罗召集围绕巴勒斯坦问题的区域妇女大会，把联盟的工作推到埃及之外。

timeline.en: Convened the Arab Feminist Congress in Cairo in December, opening it with a speech that Islamic law had given women rights that men withheld; out of the congress she led the formation of the Arab Feminist Union, became its first president and drafted its constitution in 1945.
timeline.zh: 12 月在开罗召集阿拉伯妇女大会，开幕演说指出伊斯兰教法赋予女性的权利被男性扣留；她随后推动阿拉伯女性联盟成立，出任首任主席，并于 1945 年起草章程。

timeline.en: Received the Nishan al-Kamal, Egypt's highest decoration for women, from a state that still did not let her vote.
timeline.zh: 获埃及授予女性的最高勋章「完美勋章」——授勋的国家仍不许她投票。

timeline.en: Died in Cairo on 12 December, aged 68, still president of both unions. She left a memoir of the years 1879–1924, published after her death and translated by Margot Badran as Harem Years (1986).
timeline.zh: 12 月 12 日在开罗去世，享年六十八岁，仍任两个联盟的主席。她留下记述 1879–1924 年的回忆录，在身后出版，由玛戈·巴德兰译为《闺阁岁月》（1986）。

coda.en: Egyptian women voted for the first time in 1956.
coda.zh: 1956 年，埃及妇女第一次投票。

sources.zh: 《闺阁岁月》摘录 · NYU 史料集

story.en:
Refused Arabic grammar as a girl, married at thirteen: she studied through seven years of separation, then walked into the street.

In 1919 she helped bring 300 veiled women out against British rifles. In 1923 she founded the Egyptian Feminist Union and led it 24 years: a marriage-registration age for girls, won with others; two journals; 32 demands to parliament; a pan-Arab congress in 1944.

The lifted veil is remembered; the institutions were the work. The vote she demanded in 1924 came in 1956, nine years after her death.
story.zh:
因为是女孩而学不到阿拉伯语法，十三岁被嫁人：她在七年分居中读书，然后走上街头。

1919 年她与三百名蒙面纱的妇女一同站在英军枪口下；1923 年创立埃及女性联盟并领导了二十四年：与他人一道争得女孩的婚姻登记年龄，办了两份刊物，向议会递交三十二项诉求，1944 年召集泛阿拉伯妇女大会。

人们记得她掀开面纱的画面；她建立的机构才是她的事业。她 1924 年要求的选举权，在她去世九年后的 1956 年才到来。

era.zh: 殖民地时期 · 新西兰

intro.en: From 1887 she ran the Women's Christian Temperance Union's franchise campaign: she co-ordinated the local branches, organised three years of petitions and wrote the pamphlets that argued the case, while allies in Parliament carried the bills. On 19 September 1893 New Zealand became the first self-governing country to give women the parliamentary vote; ten weeks later 90,290 women voted in the general electorates. She then edited a women's paper and led the National Council of Women, pressing for economic as well as political equality.
intro.zh: 1887 年起，她主持妇女基督教节制会的选举权运动：统筹各地分会，连续三年组织请愿，撰写小册子陈述理据，议会里的盟友则推动法案通过。1893 年 9 月 19 日，新西兰成为首个赋予女性议会选举权的自治国家；十周之后，90,290 名女性在普通选区投下选票。此后她主编妇女刊物、领导全国妇女理事会，把诉求从投票权延伸到经济平等。

timeline.en: She landed at Lyttelton from the ship Matoaka with her widowed mother and siblings, aged about 21, and settled in Christchurch.
timeline.zh: 她随守寡的母亲和兄弟姐妹乘马托卡号抵达利特尔顿，时年约 21 岁，在基督城定居。

timeline.en: After the American organiser Mary Leavitt's tour, she became a founding member of the New Zealand Women's Christian Temperance Union, one of the organisational bases of the suffrage campaign.
timeline.zh: 美国组织者玛丽·莱维特来访之后，她成为新西兰妇女基督教节制会的创始会员；这个组织后来成为选举权运动的重要基础。

timeline.en: She was appointed the union's national superintendent of franchise and legislation and built its suffrage campaign: co-ordinating local branches, writing pamphlets and letters to the press, and lobbying politicians.
timeline.zh: 她被任命为节制会全国选举权与立法部总监，着手建立争取选举权的运动：统筹各地分会，撰写小册子和报刊来信，游说政治人物。

timeline.en: Her leaflet 'Ten Reasons Why the Women of New Zealand Should Vote' went to every member of the House of Representatives in May. Reason two: it had not yet been proved that women's intelligence was only equal to children's.
timeline.zh: 五月，她的传单《新西兰妇女应当投票的十条理由》送到了众议院每一位议员手中。第二条理由：尚无人证明女性的智力仅与儿童相当。

timeline.en: She organised the first two petitions, more than 9,000 signatures and then about 20,000, which allies presented in the House, and started a women's page in the national temperance paper. Each year she saw the House pass a suffrage bill, only for the Legislative Council to wreck it with amendments.
timeline.zh: 她组织了头两次请愿，签名从九千余人增至约两万人，由议会盟友在众议院提交，并在全国禁酒报刊上开设了妇女版。两年里她都看到众议院通过选举权法案，又都被立法委员会以修正案毁掉。

timeline.en: She co-ordinated the campaign of thirteen petitions, 31,872 signatures in all, nearly a quarter of the colony's adult European women; the largest roll, some 270 metres long with about 25,500 names, was presented by John Hall and unrolled across the floor of the House on 28 July, the largest petition Parliament had ever received.
timeline.zh: 她统筹了当年的请愿运动：13 份请愿书合计 31,872 个签名，约占殖民地成年欧裔女性的四分之一；其中最大的一卷长约 270 米、约有 25,500 个签名，7 月 28 日由约翰·霍尔提交，在众议院议场里展开，是议会有史以来收到的最大一份请愿书。

timeline.en: She and her fellow suffragists gave white camellias to the bill's supporters before the Council vote, 20 to 18, on 8 September; after Governor Lord Glasgow signed the Electoral Act on 19 September, giving the parliamentary vote to women aged 21 and over, Māori women included, she received the pen he had used and a telegram of concession from Premier Seddon, who had opposed her.
timeline.zh: 9 月 8 日立法委员会以 20 票对 18 票表决之前，她和同伴们把白色山茶花送给支持法案的议员；9 月 19 日总督格拉斯哥勋爵签署《选举法》，21 岁及以上的女性、包括毛利女性获得议会选举权，她收到了总督签字用的笔，以及曾反对她的总理塞登发来的认输电报。

timeline.en: With ten weeks to the election she drove the enrolment of women and by 28 November had 109,461 on the rolls; 90,290 of them voted in the general electorates that day, an 82 per cent turnout against the men's 70, and the Māori electorates voted on 20 December.
timeline.zh: 距大选只剩十周，她推动女性登记选民，到 11 月 28 日已有 109,461 名女性登记在册；当天 90,290 人在普通选区投票，投票率 82%，高于男性的 70%；毛利选区于 12 月 20 日投票。

timeline.en: She became editor of The White Ribbon, the WCTU's sixteen-page monthly, then the only New Zealand paper started, owned, edited, managed and published by women, and ran it for eight years.
timeline.zh: 她出任节制会十六页月刊《白丝带》的主编，这是当时新西兰唯一一份由女性创办、拥有、编辑、经营和出版的报纸，她主持了八年。

timeline.en: She co-founded the National Council of Women of New Zealand at its inaugural session in Christchurch in April and was elected its first president, pressing for married women's economic independence, equal wages and proportional representation.
timeline.zh: 四月，她在基督城的成立大会上与同伴共同创建新西兰全国妇女理事会，当选首任主席，推动已婚女性经济独立、同工同酬和比例代表制。

timeline.en: Ill, she resigned the editorship, travelled to England through Canada and the United States, met Carrie Chapman Catt, and had her paper read to the International Council of Women in Berlin before returning to Christchurch.
timeline.zh: 因病辞去主编一职后，她经加拿大和美国前往英国，会见了凯莉·查普曼·卡特，其论文在柏林的国际妇女理事会上被宣读，随后返回基督城。

timeline.en: With Christina Henderson, Jessie Mackay and others she began reviving the National Council of Women, dormant since 1906; at its first revived conference in 1919 her address as founding president was read for her.
timeline.zh: 她与克里斯蒂娜·亨德森、杰西·麦凯等人着手复兴自 1906 年起停摆的全国妇女理事会；1919 年复会后的首次大会上，她以创始主席身份所写的致辞由他人代为宣读。

timeline.en: She died at her home in Riccarton, Christchurch, on 13 July, a year after Elizabeth McCombs became the first woman elected to New Zealand's Parliament; women had been able to stand since 1919.
timeline.zh: 7 月 13 日，她在基督城里卡顿的家中去世，此时距伊丽莎白·麦库姆斯成为新西兰首位女议员刚满一年；女性自 1919 年起才获得参选资格。

coda.en: Her portrait has been on New Zealand's $10 banknote since 1993, beside a white camellia.
coda.zh: 1993 年起，她的肖像印在新西兰 10 元纸币上，旁边是一朵白色山茶花。

story.en:
New Zealand's law classed women with children, lunatics and convicts. From 1887 she ran the temperance union's franchise department and answered with reasons on paper and names on rolls.

Three years of petitions: over 9,000 signatures in 1891, about 20,000 in 1892, then thirteen petitions with 31,872 names in 1893, the largest a 270-metre roll unrolled across the House. She won with the branches' names and her allies' votes: the Electoral Act was signed on 19 September 1893, and ten weeks later 90,290 women voted.

“All that separates, whether of race, class, creed, or sex, is inhuman, and must be overcome.”
story.zh:
新西兰的法律把女性与儿童、精神病人和罪犯归为一类。1887 年起，她主持节制会的选举权部门，用纸上的理由和名册上的签名作答。

三年请愿：1891 年九千余人，1892 年约两万人，1893 年十三份请愿书共 31,872 个签名，其中最大的一卷长 270 米，在议会展开。她靠各地分会征集的签名和议会盟友的选票赢得了胜利：1893 年 9 月 19 日《选举法》签署；十周后，90,290 名女性投了票。

「凡是造成隔阂的东西，无论出于种族、阶级、信仰还是性别，都是不人道的，必须克服。」

era.zh: 殖民地至独立后的尼日利亚

intro.en: A teacher from Abeokuta who, with market women and fellow organisers, remade a ladies' charity club into the Abeokuta Women's Union, estimated at 20,000 members, and led it through three years of petitions, tax refusal, vigils and mocking songs until the flat-rate tax on women was suspended in April 1948 and abolished when the king left his throne in January 1949. She then built national women's organisations, tied women's rights to Nigerian independence, and campaigned for the vote and for socialism until a military raid in February 1977 left the injuries from which she died in April 1978.
intro.zh: 她是阿贝奥库塔的一名教师，与集市女商贩和同伴组织者一起，把一个太太们的慈善会改造成据估计拥有两万名会员的阿贝奥库塔妇女联盟，率领她们经历三年请愿、抗税、守夜和讥讽之歌，直到 1948 年 4 月妇女人头税暂停、1949 年 1 月国王离开王位后税被废除。此后她建立起全国性妇女组织，把妇女权利与尼日利亚独立连在一起，为选举权和社会主义奔走，直至 1977 年 2 月一场军队突袭留下的伤势在 1978 年 4 月夺去她的生命。

timeline.en: She entered Abeokuta Grammar School, a boys' school, among its earliest female pupils (six girls that year).
timeline.zh: 她进入原本只收男生的阿贝奥库塔文法学校，是该校最早的一批女生（当年共六人）。

timeline.en: She studied at Wincham Hall in Cheshire, England, met racism first-hand and socialist ideas for the first time; on returning she dropped her English names and taught at her old school.
timeline.zh: 她在英格兰柴郡的温查姆堂求学，亲身遭遇种族歧视，也初次接触社会主义思想；归国后她弃用英文名，回母校任教。

timeline.en: She started one of Nigeria's earliest nursery classes and a self-improvement club for young women.
timeline.zh: 她创办了尼日利亚最早的幼儿班之一，以及一个年轻女性的自修社。

timeline.en: Teaching market women to read, she learned of rice seizures and of a tax that took girls from age 15 while boys paid from 18; she led a campaign that stopped the seizures.
timeline.zh: 她在教集市女商贩识字时，得知当局没收她们的大米，并向十五岁起的女孩征税而男孩十八岁才交；她领导抗争，制止了没收。

timeline.en: With fellow organisers, Grace Eniola Soyinka among them, she remade the Ladies' Club as the Abeokuta Women's Union, declared its work political, opened it to market women and was elected president; membership was estimated at 20,000.
timeline.zh: 她与格蕾丝·埃尼奥拉·索因卡等组织者一起把太太会改组为阿贝奥库塔妇女联盟，宣告其工作是政治性的，向集市女商贩敞开大门并当选主席；会员据估计达两万人。

timeline.en: She sailed as the only woman in the NCNC delegation to London against the Richards Constitution, and wrote 'We had equality till Britain came' in the Daily Worker; that November she led thousands of women to the Alake's palace.
timeline.zh: 她作为尼日利亚国民会议党赴伦敦代表团中唯一的女性，反对《理查兹宪法》，并在《工人日报》发表《英国人来之前我们本是平等的》；同年十一月她率数千名妇女直抵国王宫前。

timeline.en: With parades banned, she held 'picnics' instead: up to 10,000 women camped at the palace in December 1947 singing songs that mocked the king. She kept up petitions and tax refusal until the flat-rate tax on women was suspended in April 1948, and earned the press name 'Lioness of Lisabi'.
timeline.zh: 游行被禁，她便改办「野餐」：1947 年 12 月多达一万名妇女在宫前露宿，唱着讥讽国王的歌。她坚持请愿和抗税，直到 1948 年 4 月妇女人头税暂停，并赢得报界「利萨比的母狮」之名。

timeline.en: She and the union won abolition of the women's tax and seats in local government: on 3 January the Alake Ademola II left his throne, and she took one of four women's seats on the reconstituted council. In May she extended the union into the Nigerian Women's Union.
timeline.zh: 她和联盟争得废除妇女税与地方议席：1 月 3 日阿拉凯阿德莫拉二世离位，她成为改组后议事机构四名女性成员之一。5 月她把联盟扩展为尼日利亚妇女联盟。

timeline.en: She convened 400 delegates in Abeokuta and with them founded the Federation of Nigerian Women's Societies to fight for women's votes, and became a vice-president of the Women's International Democratic Federation.
timeline.zh: 她在阿贝奥库塔召集四百名代表，与她们共同创立尼日利亚妇女团体联合会，为妇女选举权而战，并出任国际民主妇女联合会副主席。

timeline.en: She lectured in China and the Soviet Union and met Mao Zedong; the colonial government then refused to renew her passport and the United States denied her a visa, both alleging communist ties.
timeline.zh: 她赴中国和苏联演讲并会见毛泽东；殖民政府随即拒绝续发她的护照，美国也拒发签证，皆以她「与共产主义有牵连」为由。

timeline.en: Charged for inciting women against the water rate, she ran for the federal House without her party's ticket, polled 4,665 votes and was expelled. She saw the water rate on women lifted in 1960, the year Nigeria became independent, and kept campaigning.
timeline.zh: 她因「煽动妇女抗缴水费」被起诉，随后未获党内提名仍参选联邦众议院，得票 4,665 张，遭党开除。1960 年尼日利亚独立，向妇女征收的水费也在这一年取消，她继续奔走倡议。

timeline.en: She was made a Member of the Order of the Niger (1965), received an honorary doctorate of laws from the University of Ibadan (1968) and the Lenin Peace Prize (1970).
timeline.zh: 她获尼日尔勋章（1965）、伊巴丹大学名誉法学博士（1968）和列宁和平奖（1970）。

timeline.en: On 18 February 1977 about 1,000 soldiers stormed her son Fela's compound in Lagos and threw her, aged 76, from an upper-storey window. She never recovered and died at Lagos General Hospital in April 1978; market women closed their stalls for her funeral.
timeline.zh: 1977 年 2 月 18 日约一千名士兵冲进她儿子费拉在拉各斯的住所，将七十六岁的她从楼上窗口扔下。她再未康复，1978 年 4 月在拉各斯总医院去世；集市女商贩关闭摊位为她送葬。

coda.en: The campaign she led is remembered as the Abeokuta Women's Revolt; the tax on women never came back.
coda.zh: 她领导的那场运动被后人称为「阿贝奥库塔妇女起义」；妇女税从此没有再回来。

story.en:
In colonial Abeokuta girls were taxed from fifteen, boys from eighteen, and collectors stripped girls to guess their age. Ransome-Kuti, a teacher, rebuilt a ladies' charity club with fellow organisers as the Abeokuta Women's Union and opened it to the market women who paid.

The union she led: an estimated 20,000 members; 10,000 women camped at the palace in December 1947; the tax was suspended in April 1948 and abolished when the Alake left his throne on 3 January 1949.

Her motto: 'May I never let womanhood down.'
story.zh:
在殖民时期的阿贝奥库塔，女孩十五岁起纳税，男孩十八岁才交，税吏还会剥去女孩衣服来估年龄。教师兰索姆－库蒂与同伴组织者一起，把一个太太们的慈善会改造成阿贝奥库塔妇女联盟，向真正交税的集市女商贩敞开大门。

她领导的联盟据估计有两万名会员；1947 年 12 月一万名妇女在王宫前露宿；1948 年 4 月税被暂停，1949 年 1 月 3 日国王离位、税被废除。

她终生的座右铭：「愿我永不辜负女性。」

intro.en: A Brooklyn day-care director who became, in 1968, the first Black woman elected to the United States Congress, and in 1972 the first Black woman to campaign for a major party's presidential nomination. Over seven House terms she fought for domestic workers' wages, school lunches and food aid, and called herself, above every other label, 'the candidate of the people of America'.
intro.zh: 她本是布鲁克林一位托儿所主任，1968 年成为第一位当选美国国会议员的黑人女性，1972 年又成为首位竞选美国主要政党总统提名的黑人女性。七届众议员任内，她为家政工人的工资、学校午餐和食品援助奔走；在所有标签之上，她只自称「美国人民的候选人」。

timeline.en: Returned to Brooklyn at nine after four years of strict British-style schooling on her grandmother's farm in Barbados; she later credited 'Granny' with teaching her that she was 'somebody'.
timeline.zh: 九岁时结束在巴巴多斯外祖母农场四年严格的英式学校生活，回到布鲁克林。她后来说，是「外婆」让她从小就知道自己「是个人物」。

timeline.en: Graduated cum laude in sociology from Brooklyn College and took a job at a Harlem child-care centre, teaching by day while earning a master's in early-childhood education at Columbia's Teachers College in 1951.
timeline.zh: 以优等成绩从布鲁克林学院社会学专业毕业，进入哈莱姆一家托儿中心工作，白天教课，同时在哥伦比亚大学师范学院攻读幼儿教育硕士，1951 年获学位。

timeline.en: After directing two child-care centres in Brooklyn and lower Manhattan, became an educational consultant to New York City's Division of Day Care, and in 1960 helped found the Unity Democratic Club to break the Bedford-Stuyvesant party machine.
timeline.zh: 先后执掌布鲁克林和曼哈顿下城的两家托儿中心后，出任纽约市日托处教育顾问；1960 年参与创建团结民主俱乐部，向贝德福德-斯泰弗森特的党内机器发起挑战。

timeline.en: Won a seat in the New York State Assembly, the second Black woman ever to sit there. With colleagues she pushed through the SEEK programme, which opened City University places to disadvantaged students, and won unemployment insurance for domestic workers.
timeline.zh: 当选纽约州众议员，是史上第二位进入该州议会的黑人女性。她与同僚一道推动通过 SEEK 计划，为贫困学生打开纽约市立大学的大门，并为家政工人争得失业保险。

timeline.en: Running as 'Unbought and Unbossed' in a newly drawn Brooklyn district, won the primary by about 800 votes and the general election with 67 percent, becoming the first Black woman elected to the US Congress.
timeline.zh: 以「不受收买、不受操纵」为口号，在新划定的布鲁克林选区先以约 800 票之差赢下初选，再以 67% 的得票赢得大选，成为第一位当选美国国会议员的黑人女性。

timeline.en: Assigned to the Agriculture Committee, she protested to the Speaker, the caucus and the press until moved to Veterans' Affairs ('there are a lot more veterans in my district than trees'); used her first floor speech, 26 March, to oppose the Vietnam war and defence spending.
timeline.zh: 被分配到农业委员会后，她向议长、党团和媒体一路抗议，直至被调到退伍军人事务委员会——「我选区里的退伍军人可比树多得多」。3 月 26 日的首次议场发言，她公开反对越战和国防开支。

timeline.en: Became a founding member of the Congressional Black Caucus and, in July, co-founded the National Women's Political Caucus with Bella Abzug, Betty Friedan, Fannie Lou Hamer and Gloria Steinem; joined the Education and Labor Committee.
timeline.zh: 成为国会黑人党团的创始成员，7 月又与贝拉·阿布朱格、贝蒂·弗里丹、范妮·卢·哈默和格洛丽亚·斯泰纳姆共同创立全国妇女政治党团；同年进入教育与劳工委员会。

timeline.en: Announced for the Democratic presidential nomination on 25 January in a Brooklyn church, the first Black woman to campaign for a major party's nomination. Opening with about $44,000 against rivals' millions, she reached twelve primary ballots and took 152 delegate votes at the Miami convention, some released to her by other candidates' delegates.
timeline.zh: 1 月 25 日在布鲁克林一座教堂宣布竞选民主党总统提名，成为首位竞选主要政党总统提名的黑人女性。对手坐拥数百万美元，她以约 4.4 万美元起步，却登上十二个州的初选选票，在迈阿密党代会上获得 152 张代表票——其中一部分来自其他候选人释放的代表。

timeline.en: Championed extending the federal minimum wage to domestic workers, which became law in the 1974 Fair Labor Standards Act amendments; in 1975 widened eligibility for free and reduced-price school lunches and helped override President Ford's veto, while pressing to expand food stamps and the WIC nutrition programme.
timeline.zh: 力推将家政工人纳入联邦最低工资保护，1974 年《公平劳动标准法》修正案使之成为法律；1975 年扩大学校免费及减价午餐的受益范围，并参与推翻福特总统的否决，同时持续争取扩大食品券和 WIC 妇幼营养计划。

timeline.en: Became the first Black woman to sit on the House Rules Committee, served as Secretary of the Democratic Caucus (1977–81) and helped found the Congressional Women's Caucus.
timeline.zh: 成为第一位进入众议院规则委员会的黑人女性，出任民主党党团秘书（1977–81），并参与创立国会妇女党团。

timeline.en: Worked with Walter Fauntroy on a task force on Haitian refugees and in 1980 introduced legislation on their treatment.
timeline.zh: 与沃尔特·福恩特罗伊共同开展海地难民问题工作组的工作，并于 1980 年提出关于难民待遇的法案。

timeline.en: Left Congress after seven terms, saying 'Shirley Chisholm would like to have a little life of her own', and took up the Purington Chair at Mount Holyoke College, teaching courses including The Black Woman in America.
timeline.zh: 七届任期后离开国会，留下一句「雪莉·奇泽姆也想有一点自己的生活」，随即受聘为曼荷莲学院普灵顿讲席教授，开设「美国黑人女性」等课程。

timeline.en: Died on 1 January in Ormond Beach, Florida, aged 80. Her vault in Buffalo bears three words: 'Unbought and Unbossed'.
timeline.zh: 1 月 1 日在佛罗里达州奥蒙德比奇去世，享年 80 岁。她在布法罗的墓穴上只刻着一句话：「不受收买，不受操纵」。

coda.en: In November 2015 President Obama awarded her the Presidential Medal of Freedom.
coda.zh: 2015 年 11 月，奥巴马总统追授她总统自由勋章。

story.en:
Washington put the new Brooklyn congresswoman on the Agriculture Committee. She refused to be a 'good soldier', took the fight to the caucus and the press, and won a seat on Veterans' Affairs.

Over seven terms she helped extend the minimum wage to domestic workers, widened free school lunches over a presidential veto, and in 1972 launched a presidential run with about $44,000, carrying 152 delegate votes into the convention.

'I am the candidate of the people of America' — everyone, not a denial of being Black or a woman.
story.zh:
华盛顿把这位来自贝德福德-斯泰弗森特的新科众议员塞进了农业委员会。她拒绝做「听话的兵」，把这场仗打到党团和媒体面前，最终换来退伍军人事务委员会的席位。

七届任期里，她推动把最低工资扩展到家政工人，顶着总统否决扩大了学校免费午餐；1972 年，她以约 4.4 万美元起步竞选总统，把 152 张代表票带进了党代会。

「我是美国人民的候选人」——这是向所有人发出的主张，不是否认自己是黑人或女性。

intro.en: A Sorbonne-trained naturalist who entered Brazil's National Museum by public examination in 1919 and used that standing to help win Brazilian women the vote in 1932. In 1945 she went to San Francisco with the Brazilian delegation and, with Minerva Bernardino and other delegates, pressed the equal rights of men and women into the opening words of the United Nations Charter. She collected and described Brazilian frogs for more than half a century, and in 1973 gathered that work into Brazilian Species of Hyla.
intro.zh: 她在索邦受训成为博物学家，1919 年经公开考试进入巴西国家博物馆，并以这份身份推动巴西女性在 1932 年取得选举权。1945 年，她随巴西代表团前往旧金山，与多米尼加的米内尔瓦·贝尔纳迪诺等代表一道，把「男女平等权利」写进了《联合国宪章》的开篇。她采集、研究巴西蛙类五十余年，1973 年将这些工作汇成专著《巴西雨蛙属物种》。

timeline.en: Graduated from the Sorbonne in natural sciences, zoology, botany and chemistry, came home to Rio, and on 28 December published a letter in Revista da Semana calling for a society of Brazilian women fit to take up the political duties the future would have to share with them.
timeline.zh: 从索邦大学毕业，所学涵盖自然科学、动物学、植物学与化学；回到里约后，于 12 月 28 日在《每周杂志》发表公开信，呼吁组建一个由巴西女性组成的团体，好有能力担起未来终将与她们分享的政治职责。

timeline.en: Sat the public examination for secretary of the Museu Nacional, was appointed by decree of 3 September and took office the next day — by the Chamber of Deputies' account the second woman in the Brazilian federal civil service. She founded the Liga para a Emancipação Intelectual da Mulher around the same time; official sources give 1919, her own letters 1920.
timeline.zh: 参加巴西国家博物馆秘书一职的公开考试，9 月 3 日经法令任命，次日到任——依巴西众议院的记载，是进入联邦公职系统的第二位女性。前后她创办「妇女智识解放联盟」：官方资料记为 1919 年，她本人的信件则写作 1920 年。

timeline.en: Went to Baltimore in April for the First Pan-American Conference of Women and was elected a vice-president of the association it formed; on 9 August she rebuilt her league as the Federação Brasileira pelo Progresso Feminino, and in December convened its first national conference in Rio on schooling, women's work, mothers and the vote.
timeline.zh: 4 月赴巴尔的摩出席第一届泛美妇女大会，并当选新成立协会的副主席；8 月 9 日，她把原来的联盟改组为「巴西女性进步联合会」，12 月在里约召开首届全国大会，议题涵盖教育、女性劳动、母亲保护与选举权。

timeline.en: Led the Federation through the next decade — and on until 1942 — lobbying senators, organising professional women and taking the suffrage case to the press and to inter-American meetings through years of political upheaval.
timeline.zh: 此后十年（她一直领导联合会到 1942 年），她在政局动荡中游说参议员、组织职业女性，把争取选举权的主张带上报刊，也带进泛美会议。

timeline.en: Saw the campaign land: Brazil's first Electoral Code, decreed on 24 February, made an elector of 'the citizen over 21 years of age, without distinction of sex'. It was not universal suffrage — people who could not read and write stayed excluded, and women's electoral duties differed from men's — so she at once founded the Liga Eleitoral Independente to register and organise the new women voters.
timeline.zh: 她多年奔走终于落地：2 月 24 日颁布的巴西第一部《选举法》规定「年满 21 岁的公民，不分性别，均为选民」。这还不是全民普选——不识字者仍被排除，女性的选举义务也与男性不同——她随即创办「独立选举联盟」，为新登记的女性选民做组织工作。

timeline.en: Took a law degree at the University of Rio de Janeiro at thirty-nine, then argued the constitutional case for women's rights as the Constituent Assembly sat; the constitution promulgated on 16 July 1934 kept women's suffrage in the text, making voting compulsory for women in paid public office.
timeline.zh: 三十九岁时在里约热内卢大学取得法学学位，随后在制宪会议期间为女性权利提出宪法层面的论证；1934 年 7 月 16 日颁布的宪法把女性选举权写入正文，并规定担任有薪公职的女性须投票。

timeline.en: Took her seat in the Chamber of Deputies on 28 July, having finished first alternate in the 1934 election, and introduced the Estatuto da Mulher — equal pay, three months' maternity leave, shorter hours, and an end to rules requiring a husband's consent for a married woman to work. She chaired the special commission on it and carried it through a first reading in October 1937.
timeline.zh: 她在 1934 年大选中位列第一候补，7 月 28 日正式就任联邦众议员，并提出《妇女法案》：同工同酬、三个月产假、缩短工时，并废除已婚女性就业须经丈夫同意的规定。她主持该法案的特别委员会，1937 年 10 月推动其通过一读。

timeline.en: Lost the mandate on 10 November when the Estado Novo closed Congress; the bill never became law. She returned to her duties at the Museu Nacional, stood in briefly for the head of its botany section in 1938, and kept collecting and publishing on Brazilian amphibians through the dictatorship.
timeline.zh: 11 月 10 日，新国家体制关闭国会，她的议员资格随之终止，法案也未能成为法律。她回到国家博物馆，1938 年短期代理植物学部负责人，并在独裁年代里继续采集、发表关于巴西两栖类的研究。

timeline.en: Sat in Brazil's delegation at the San Francisco conference and spoke to Commission I's second committee on 15 June. With Minerva Bernardino and the other Latin American delegates, and over the reluctance of some delegates from the United States and Britain, she got women named in the Charter: the preamble affirms 'the equal rights of men and women', and Article 8 opens every United Nations organ to both on equal terms.
timeline.zh: 她作为巴西代表团成员出席旧金山会议，6 月 15 日在第一委员会第二小组发言。她与贝尔纳迪诺等拉美代表一起，顶住美、英两国部分代表的保留意见，让「女性」二字进入宪章：序言申明「男女平等权利」，第八条则规定联合国各机关对男女平等开放。

timeline.en: Signed the Charter on 26 June as one of only four women to sign it. She had also pressed for a standing United Nations body on women; the conference declined, and the Commission on the Status of Women was created the following June without her on it.
timeline.zh: 6 月 26 日在宪章上签字，是在宪章上签字的仅有四位女性之一。她还力主设立一个常设的联合国妇女机构，会议未予采纳；妇女地位委员会于次年 6 月成立，她并不在其中。

timeline.en: Kept both careers going: she represented Brazil at inter-American and United Nations meetings while continuing her museum work on Brazilian frogs, and said openly that her diplomatic work had gone unrecognised.
timeline.zh: 她把两条路都走了下去：一面代表巴西出席泛美与联合国的会议，一面继续在博物馆研究巴西蛙类；她也公开表示，自己在外交上的工作始终未被承认。

timeline.en: Published Brazilian Species of Hyla at seventy-nine, bringing together her taxonomic and natural-history work on Brazilian tree frogs — a lifetime's science, not a credential beside her politics.
timeline.zh: 七十九岁时出版《巴西雨蛙属物种》，汇集她对巴西树蛙分类与自然史的研究——这是一生的科学工作，而不只是她政治活动旁的一纸学历。

timeline.en: Travelled to Mexico City at eighty to attend the United Nations International Women's Year conference, fifty-seven years after her first letter to a Rio magazine.
timeline.zh: 八十岁那年前往墨西哥城，出席联合国「国际妇女年」世界大会——距她写给里约那家杂志的第一封公开信，已过去五十七年。

timeline.en: Died in Rio de Janeiro on 16 September, aged 82.
timeline.zh: 9 月 16 日在里约热内卢去世，享年 82 岁。

coda.en: In 2023 UNESCO inscribed her papers, 'Feminism, science and politics — Bertha Lutz's legacy', on its Memory of the World registers.
coda.zh: 2023 年，联合国教科文组织将她的档案「女性主义、科学与政治——贝尔塔·卢茨的遗产」列入世界记忆名录。

story.en:
Brazil in 1918 had little room for a woman with a Sorbonne science degree. She sat the National Museum's public examination anyway, entered as its secretary, and turned a laboratory and a civil-service salary into a base for a suffrage campaign.

She built the Federação Brasileira pelo Progresso Feminino in 1922, won the vote by decree on 24 February 1932 — a vote still closed to those who could not read — took a seat in the Chamber in 1936, and in 1945, alongside Minerva Bernardino and other delegates, argued 'the equal rights of men and women' into the UN Charter.

She made knowledge as well as law: for more than half a century she collected and described Brazilian frogs, and in 1973 gathered that work into Brazilian Species of Hyla.
story.zh:
1918 年的巴西，几乎容不下一个拿着索邦理学学位的女人。她照样去考国家博物馆的公开招考，以秘书身份进了馆，把一间实验室和一份公职薪水变成争取选举权的据点。

1922 年她创建巴西女性进步联合会，1932 年 2 月 24 日争到以法令落地的选举权——不识字者仍被挡在门外——1936 年坐进众议院，1945 年又与贝尔纳迪诺等代表一起，把「男女平等权利」推进了《联合国宪章》。

她既争权利，也创造知识：半个多世纪里，她采集、描述巴西蛙类，1973 年将这些工作汇成《巴西雨蛙属物种》。

intro.en: Kept out of school as a girl, Begum Rokeya learned Bangla and English at home with her sister and brother, and used them to argue, in essays, satire and fiction, that women's seclusion was a man-made arrangement and not a law of religion. From 1909 she built and ran a girls' school in Bhagalpur and then Calcutta, walking door to door for its pupils and training its teachers, founded a Muslim women's association in 1916, and over more than twenty years grew the school into a high school.
intro.zh: 贝古姆·罗基亚小时候被挡在学堂之外，她在家里跟着姐姐和哥哥学会了孟加拉语和英语，并用这两种语言写散文、讽刺小说与长篇小说，论证女性的深闺幽禁是人为的安排，而非宗教的律法。1909 年起，她在博格尔布尔、继而在加尔各答创办并经营一所女子学校，挨家挨户去说服家长送女儿入学，亲自培训教师；1916 年创立穆斯林妇女协会；二十多年间把学校办成了一所中学。

timeline.en: Refused schooling while her brothers were sent to college in Calcutta, she learned Bangla and English at home with her elder sister Karimunnesa and her eldest brother — by scholarly accounts at night — in a family that thought neither language fit for girls.
timeline.zh: 兄长们被送去加尔各答上学，她却不许进学堂；她在家里跟着姐姐卡里穆内萨和大哥学会了孟加拉语和英语——据学界的记述是在夜里学的——而在这个家里，这两种语言都被认为不适合女孩。

timeline.en: Began publishing in the Bengali journals: one account gives her first printed piece as 'Pipasa' (Thirst) in Nabaprabha in 1902, and from about 1903 she wrote in Nabanoor as Mrs R. S. Hossain.
timeline.zh: 开始在孟加拉语刊物上发表文章：一种说法认为她最早印出的作品是 1902 年刊于《新曙光》的《渴》，约自 1903 年起，她以「R·S·侯赛因夫人」之名在《新光》上写作。

timeline.en: Published the first volume of Matichur, her collected essays on women's condition, arguing that ignorance, not religion, kept women dependent; the second volume followed in 1922.
timeline.zh: 出版散文集《珍珠碎》第一卷，论述女性的处境，指出使女性依附于人的是无知而非宗教；第二卷于 1922 年问世。

timeline.en: Wrote 'Sultana's Dream' in English and saw it printed in The Indian Ladies' Magazine in Madras — a Ladyland where men are shut into the mardana, kitchens cook by piped sunlight, balloons pull the rain out of the sky, and an invading army is turned back by concentrated sun. Among the earliest feminist speculative fiction from South Asia, it came out as a book in 1908, and she later put it into Bangla herself.
timeline.zh: 她用英文写下《苏丹娜之梦》，刊于马德拉斯的《印度女性杂志》——那是一个「女儿国」：男人被关进「男眷院」，厨房用导管引来的日光做饭，气球把雨水从天上抽走，入侵的军队被聚焦的阳光逼退。这是南亚最早的女性主义幻想文学之一，1908 年结集成书，后来她又亲自把它译成孟加拉文。

timeline.en: Opened the Sakhawat Memorial Girls' School at Bhagalpur on 1 October with five pupils, using a bequest her husband had left for a girls' school before his death that May, and organised and ran it herself; a property dispute with his family soon drove her out of the town.
timeline.zh: 10 月 1 日在博格尔布尔开办萨卡瓦特纪念女子学校，只有五名学生，用的是丈夫当年 5 月去世前留下的一笔办女校的遗赠，学校由她一手组织、经营；不久，与夫家的财产纠纷把她逼出了这座城市。

timeline.en: Reopened the school on 16 March at 13 Waliullah Lane in Calcutta with eight newly enrolled pupils, and ran it for the rest of her life — moving it from address to address as it outgrew them.
timeline.zh: 3 月 16 日，她在加尔各答瓦利乌拉巷 13 号重开学校，新招了八名学生；此后她一直经营到去世——校舍容不下了就一处处地搬。

timeline.en: Went from house to house persuading guardians to let their daughters attend, promising that purdah would be kept at the school, and put curtained horse-carriages on the road so girls could travel there and back unseen.
timeline.zh: 她挨家挨户去说服监护人让女儿上学，承诺学校里会守住深闺之礼，又在路上备下带帘的马车，让女孩们来回都不被人看见。

timeline.en: Founded the Anjuman-e-Khawateen-e-Islam, a Muslim women's association that paid school fees for many girls, sheltered orphans and the destitute, gave money to widows and set up small businesses so that women could earn for themselves.
timeline.zh: 创立穆斯林妇女协会「安珠曼」，为许多女孩支付学费，收容孤儿与无依者，接济寡妇，并开办小本生意，让女性能够自己挣钱。

timeline.en: Trained her own teachers because competent women teachers were scarce in Calcutta, and pressed the government for a training school for Muslim women; one opened in the city that year.
timeline.zh: 加尔各答缺少合格的女教师，她便亲自培训自己的教师，并向政府争取开办穆斯林女子师范学校；当年市内开办了一所。

timeline.en: Published Padmarag, her only full-length novel, set in Tarini Bhavan — a community founded and run by women where Hindu, Brahmo, Muslim and Christian women teach, make crafts and nurse the sick, each telling the story of the marriage or family that broke her.
timeline.zh: 出版她唯一的长篇小说《红宝石》，故事设在「塔里尼堂」——一个由女性创办、由女性管理的共同体，印度教、梵社、穆斯林与基督徒女性在那里教书、做手工、照料病人，各自讲出那段毁了自己的婚姻或家庭。

timeline.en: Gave the President's Address at the First Bengal Women's Education Conference in Calcutta, defending women's right to learn; a later English rendering has her telling the hall she had been crying for twenty years for the lowliest creature in India — the Indian woman — and answering the opponents of girls' schooling on their own religious ground.
timeline.zh: 在加尔各答第一届孟加拉妇女教育大会上作主席演说，为女性受教育的权利辩护；据后出的英文转述，她告诉全场，二十年来她一直为印度最卑微的生灵——印度女性——而呼号，并站在反对者自己的宗教立场上驳斥他们反对女子上学的理由。

timeline.en: Published Abarodhbasini (The Secluded Women), forty-seven short reported anecdotes, told with a documentary eye and a satirist's edge, of what extreme purdah did to women's bodies and lives — in the year Banglapedia gives for her school's rise to a high school.
timeline.zh: 出版《幽居的女人们》，以四十七则短小的纪实轶事，带着纪录的眼光和讽刺的锋芒，记下极端的深闺制度对女性身体与生活的伤害；据孟加拉国家百科，同一年她的学校升格为高级中学。

timeline.en: Died in Calcutta on 9 December, aged fifty-two, of heart failure, still head of the school she had opened with five pupils twenty-three years earlier.
timeline.zh: 12 月 9 日，她在加尔各答因心力衰竭去世，时年五十二岁；她仍是那所学校的校长——二十三年前，它只有五名学生。

coda.en: Bangladesh observes 9 December as Rokeya Day; in 2024, on Bangladesh's nomination, UNESCO's Memory of the World Committee for Asia and the Pacific inscribed Sultana's Dream on its regional register.
coda.zh: 孟加拉国把 12 月 9 日定为罗基亚日；2024 年，经孟加拉国提名，联合国教科文组织世界记忆亚太委员会将《苏丹娜之梦》列入其地区名录。

story.en:
She was kept home while her brothers went to college. She learned Bangla and English anyway, and wrote.

In 1905 she published a satire in English in which men sit indoors and women run the state. In 1909 she opened a school with five pupils; in 1911 she reopened it in Calcutta with eight, canvassed guardians door to door, trained its teachers, and by 1931 had a high school. In between she founded a women's association, wrote a novel, and set down forty-seven cases of what seclusion did to women.

On the page she asked what the world would look like turned over. In the school she widened what girls could actually learn. Neither was the lesser work.
story.zh:
她被留在家里，哥哥们却去上学。她还是学会了孟加拉语和英语，并且开始写作。

1905 年，她用英文发表了一篇讽刺小说：男人待在屋里，女人治理国家。1909 年，她用五名学生办起一所学校；1911 年，她在加尔各答重新开校，新招八名学生，挨家挨户去说服监护人，亲手培训教师，到 1931 年已办成一所中学。其间她创立了妇女协会，写了一部长篇小说，记下了四十七则深闺制度伤害女性的实例。

在纸上，她追问世界颠倒过来会是什么样；在学校里，她扩大了女孩现实中能学到的东西。两样都不是次要的事业。

latin: Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz

intro.en: No university in New Spain admitted girls. By her own account she asked at six or seven to be sent to Mexico City in boy's clothes, was refused, and taught herself from her grandfather's books and then from her own; in 1669 she took the veil for the reason she gave herself: she wanted no obligatory occupation to hamper the freedom of her study. From one cell in Mexico City she wrote comedies, sacramental plays, verse for the cathedrals' religious festivals, court commissions and Primero Sueño, a long poem on the mind's pursuit of knowledge and its limits; her collected poems were printed in Madrid in 1689 and reprinted across the Spanish empire while she lived. When the Bishop of Puebla put her private theological critique into print without her knowledge and urged her to leave secular letters for sacred study, she answered with the Respuesta a Sor Filotea — among the earliest sustained defences of women's right to learn written in the Americas.
intro.zh: 新西班牙的大学不收女孩。据她自己回忆，六七岁时她曾求母亲给她换上男装送她去墨西哥城读书，没能如愿，便先读外祖父的藏书，后来读自己的藏书，全部自学。1669 年她入修道院，理由是她自己写下的：不愿有任何固定差事妨碍她读书的自由。在墨西哥城的一间修道室里，她写喜剧、写圣体剧、为主教座堂写宗教节庆颂歌、接宫廷订件，写下长诗《初梦》——写心智追索知识及其限度；她的诗集 1689 年就在马德里付印，生前在西班牙帝国各地一再重版。当普埃布拉主教未经她知情把她私下写的神学评论印出来、还劝她放下俗世文章专事宗教学问时，她写下《答菲洛特亚修女书》回应——这是美洲最早系统论证女性求知权利的文字之一。

timeline.en: By her own account in the Respuesta, she tagged along to the neighbourhood dame-school where an older sister was being taught, told the teacher her mother had ordered a lesson for her too, and learned to read. She kept it secret, expecting a whipping for having done it without permission.
timeline.zh: 据她在《答书》中的自述，姐姐去街坊的女塾念书，她跟了去，骗老师说母亲也吩咐了要教她，就这样学会了认字。她把这事瞒了下来，怕大人因她「未经许可」而打她。

timeline.en: Hearing that Mexico City had a University, she wore her mother down with pleading, as she later recalled: change my clothes, send me there, let me study. No university took girls, and her mother refused; she worked through her grandfather's books instead, and neither punishment nor scolding was enough to stop her.
timeline.zh: 听说墨西哥城有大学，她缠着母亲不放——这是她成年后的回忆：给我换身衣裳，送我去，让我读书。大学不收女孩，母亲也没有答应；她转而把外祖父的藏书一本本啃完，打也好、骂也好，都拦不住她。

timeline.en: She entered the viceregal palace as lady-in-waiting to the vicereine Leonor Carreto and stayed nearly three years, known across the court for her learning. By her biographer Diego Calleja's later account she faced some forty scholars of the university and the city, assembled to test whether her knowledge was infused or acquired, and answered them all.
timeline.zh: 她进入总督府，成为总督夫人莱昂诺尔·卡雷托的侍女，待了将近三年，以学识闻名宫廷。据她的传记作者迪耶戈·卡列哈后来记载，宫中曾召集大学与城中约四十位学者当面考校她，看她的学问是「天授」还是「习得」，她一一作答。

timeline.en: She entered the Discalced Carmelite convent of San José on 14 August, taking the name de la Cruz, and left on 28 November without professing; later biographies tie the departure to her health and to a rule too severe for the life of study she wanted.
timeline.zh: 8 月 14 日，她进入赤足加尔默罗会的圣若瑟修道院，取会名「德拉克鲁斯」；11 月 28 日未及发愿便离开——后来的传记把这归于她的健康，也归于那里清规太严，容不下她想过的读书生活。

timeline.en: She professed at the Hieronymite convent of San Jerónimo, having found a sponsor for the dowry of 3,000 pesos, and signed the convent's book in her own hand. Her reason, set down years later, was partly her own: she refused marriage outright, and wanted no obligatory occupation to hamper the freedom of her study — while taking on the vows and duties of the house with it.
timeline.zh: 她在圣哲罗姆会的圣赫罗尼莫修道院正式发愿。三千比索的入会嫁资是她自己张罗到人代付的；修道院的名册上，是她亲笔签的名。多年后她写下自己的理由，其中一层是她自己的：她断然不愿结婚，也不愿有任何固定差事妨碍她读书的自由——同时她也接下了修道生活的誓愿与院中职责。

timeline.en: She designed the allegorical programme and wrote the text of the Neptuno alegórico, the triumphal arch that received the incoming viceroys, and was paid 200 gold pesos for it by the cathedral chapter of Mexico — one of the commissions from which she built an income, and a library, of her own.
timeline.zh: 她为迎接新任总督的凯旋门《寓意的尼普顿》拟定寓意方案并撰写配套文字；墨西哥主教座堂教士会为此付给她两百枚金比索。靠着这类订件，她攒下了自己的收入，也攒下了自己的藏书。

timeline.en: She had the comedy Los empeños de una casa staged, and went on supplying villancicos for the religious festivals of the cathedrals of Mexico, Puebla and Oaxaca, sacramental plays including El divino Narciso, court verse, and the redondillas 'Hombres necios que acusáis' that turn the charge of vice back on the men who make it.
timeline.zh: 她的喜剧《一屋之难》上演；此外她持续为墨西哥、普埃布拉、瓦哈卡三地主教座堂写宗教节庆颂歌，写圣体剧（包括《神圣的纳西索》）、宫廷诗，也写下那首《愚蠢的男人啊，你们指责……》，把指责女人的罪名原样掷回给男人。

timeline.en: She sent a manuscript of her poems to Madrid with the departing vicereine María Luisa Manrique de Lara, who saw it through the press, and it was printed as Inundación castálida. It was reprinted again and again, carrying the work of a nun in New Spain across Spain and its empire while she was still alive.
timeline.zh: 她把一份诗稿托离任的总督夫人玛丽亚·路易莎·曼里克·德拉腊带往马德里，由她支持付印，以《卡斯塔利亚的洪流》为名出版，此后一版再版——一位新西班牙修女的作品，在她生前就传遍西班牙及其帝国。

timeline.en: She had written out her objections to a sermon by the Jesuit António Vieira for one reader, in private. She found them in print that November under a title she had not chosen, the Carta Atenagórica — 'so entirely without my knowledge', she wrote afterwards. She had not paid for the printing either, and she found bound to it a preface signed 'Sor Filotea' urging her to leave secular letters for sacred learning.
timeline.zh: 她原本只是私下写给一个人看，逐条反驳耶稣会士维埃拉的一篇布道。这年 11 月，她却发现文章已经印出来了，还被冠上一个她没取过的名字《雅典娜之信》——事后她写道，这事「全然不曾让我知道」；命名的人、出资的人都另有其人，卷首还附了一封署名「菲洛特亚修女」的信，劝她放下俗世文章，专事宗教学问。

timeline.en: She answered from her cell with the Respuesta a Sor Filotea de la Cruz: her own intellectual life laid out as evidence, the learned women of the past called as witnesses, and an argument that study belongs to any mind fit for it, that learned older women should be the ones teaching girls, and that knowledge lives in ordinary observation — what can we women know, she asks, but kitchen philosophies? She did not print it; it passed from hand to hand in manuscript.
timeline.zh: 她在修道室里写下《答菲洛特亚修女书》作答：把自己一生的求知经历当作证据摆出来，把历代有学问的女性一一请来作证，论证学问属于任何配得上它的头脑，论证有学问的年长女性才该是教导女孩的人，也论证知识就活在日常观察里——她反问，我们女人除了「厨房里的哲学」还能懂什么呢？这封信她没有付印，只以手抄本辗转流传。

timeline.en: She saw the second volume of her works printed at Seville, carrying Primero Sueño, her long poem on the soul's night flight after knowledge and the limits it meets — the only thing, she said, she ever wrote for her own pleasure.
timeline.zh: 她的作品第二卷在塞维利亚印行，收入长诗《初梦》：写灵魂在夜里飞升、追索知识，也写它撞上的界限。她说，这是她此生唯一一篇纯为自己高兴而写的东西。

timeline.en: She composed the Enigmas, riddle-poems for a literary circle of Portuguese nuns who called themselves the Casa del Placer. A manuscript collection dated 1695 preserves them, so her work went on circulating among learned women to the end — though the date of the copy does not show when she wrote each poem.
timeline.zh: 她为一群自称「欢愉之家」的葡萄牙修女文学圈写下《谜题》组诗。一份标着 1695 年的手抄文集保存了它们，可见直到最后，她的作品仍在有学问的女性之间流传——但抄本的日期并不能说明每首诗写于何时。

timeline.en: In the month she completed twenty-five years in the habit she wrote a group of penitential papers, and in the weeks that followed signed a protestation of faith with her own blood. Her books and her musical and scientific instruments went to the Archbishop of Mexico to be sold for the poor in the famines and epidemics that had run since 1690; whether she surrendered them freely or under pressure is still argued.
timeline.zh: 这一年正是她受戒满二十五年之时。她写下一组忏悔文书，并以自己的血签下一份信仰之誓。她的藏书、乐器与科学仪器交给墨西哥大主教变卖，所得用于赈济穷人——1690 年以来饥荒与瘟疫不断。她是自愿交出，还是被迫交出，至今争论不休。

timeline.en: When an epidemic reached San Jerónimo she nursed the sick nuns of her house, caught the disease, and died there.
timeline.zh: 疫病传入圣赫罗尼莫修道院，她照料染病的同修，自己也染上了，死在院中。

coda.en: Her Respuesta stayed in manuscript while she lived. It was printed at Madrid in 1700, in Fama y obras póstumas del Fénix de México.
coda.zh: 《答菲洛特亚修女书》生前始终只是手稿。1700 年，它收入《墨西哥凤凰的声名与遗作》在马德里刊行。

No university took girls. By her own account she asked at six or seven to be sent in boy's clothes, was refused, and read her grandfather's library instead; in 1669 she took the veil for a reason she stated herself: no obligatory occupation to hamper the freedom of her study.

From one cell she wrote comedies, sacramental plays, festival verse and Primero Sueño, built one of the largest libraries in New Spain, and had her poems printed in Madrid in 1689 and reprinted across the empire while she lived.

1691, in the Respuesta a Sor Filotea, on what women may know: 'Had Aristotle cooked, he would have written a great deal more.'
story.zh:
大学不收女子。据她自己回忆，六七岁时她求家里给她换上男装送她去，没能如愿，便改读外祖父的藏书。1669 年她入修道院，理由是她自己写下的：不愿有任何固定差事妨碍她读书的自由。

在一间修道室里，她写喜剧、写圣体剧、写节庆颂歌，写下《初梦》，攒起新西班牙数一数二的藏书，1689 年又把诗集印到了马德里，生前一版再版。

1691 年，她在《答菲洛特亚修女书》里谈女人能懂什么：「倘若亚里士多德下过厨房，他会写得多得多。」

era.zh: 德意志帝国 · 魏玛共和国

intro.en: Clara Zetkin argued from 1889 that women's emancipation rests on their own paid work and economic independence, not on being protected out of the labour market. She edited Die Gleichheit for twenty-five years, was elected in 1907 to head the international organisation of socialist women, and in August 1910 helped carry the German delegation's Copenhagen motion for an annual International Women's Day. She opposed the First World War and convened the Bern women's conference against it in 1915. A communist deputy in the Reichstag from 1920, she opened the newly elected chamber in August 1932 as its oldest member and called for a united front of working people against fascism.
intro.zh: 从 1889 年起，克拉拉·蔡特金就主张：妇女解放的基础是她们自己的有酬劳动和经济独立，而不是被「保护」着排除在劳动市场之外。她主编《平等报》二十五年，1907 年当选社会主义妇女国际组织的负责人，1910 年 8 月在哥本哈根参与推动德国代表团设立一年一度国际妇女节的动议。她反对第一次世界大战，1915 年召集了伯尔尼反战妇女会议。1920 年起她以共产党人身份进入国会，1932 年 8 月以最年长议员的身份主持新一届国会开幕，呼吁劳动者结成反法西斯的统一战线。

timeline.en: Joined the Socialist Workers' Party the year Bismarck's Anti-Socialist Laws came into force, after training as a teacher in Leipzig from 1874; her family broke with her over it, and she supported herself as a governess and tutor.
timeline.zh: 1874 年起在莱比锡读师范，1878 年——俾斯麦《反社会党人法》生效那一年——她加入社会主义工人党；家里因此与她决裂，她靠做家庭教师和私人教师谋生。

timeline.en: Left Germany for Zurich to work on the party's exile paper Der Sozialdemokrat, and in November moved on to Paris, where she lived by translating and writing for eight years and raised two sons.
timeline.zh: 她离开德国前往苏黎世，为流亡中的党报《社会民主党人报》工作；同年 11 月转赴巴黎，靠翻译和写作维持八年生计，并抚养两个儿子。

timeline.en: On 19 July she addressed the founding congress of the Second International in Paris on women's work, against socialists who wanted women barred from the factories to protect men's wages: work, she argued, is the indispensable condition of a woman's economic independence, and without it she stays subjugated.
timeline.zh: 7 月 19 日，她在巴黎第二国际成立大会上就妇女劳动发言，反驳那些主张禁止妇女进工厂、以保住男工工资的社会主义者：她说，劳动是妇女经济独立不可或缺的条件，没有它，妇女就仍处于被奴役的地位。

timeline.en: Took charge of the socialist women's paper in January and ran it as Die Gleichheit until 1917, taking it from a few thousand copies to about 70,000 by 1907 and 124,000 by 1914.
timeline.zh: 1 月起主持社会主义妇女报刊，以《平等报》之名一直办到 1917 年：发行量从几千份增至 1907 年的约七万份、1914 年的十二万四千份。

timeline.en: At the first International Conference of Socialist Women in Stuttgart she carried the resolution demanding women's suffrage without property or education qualifications, and was elected to head the new International Socialist Women's Secretariat, with Die Gleichheit as its organ.
timeline.zh: 在斯图加特第一届国际社会主义妇女大会上，她推动通过了要求妇女选举权、不设财产与学历门槛的决议，并当选新设立的国际社会主义妇女书记处负责人，《平等报》成为其机关刊物。

timeline.en: On 27 August, at the second International Conference of Socialist Women in Copenhagen, she helped carry the German delegation's motion for an annual Women's Day, building on the Woman's Day that socialist women in the United States had held since 1909; some 100 delegates from 17 countries adopted it. The resolution named no date — that was left to each country.
timeline.zh: 8 月 27 日，在哥本哈根第二届国际社会主义妇女大会上，她参与推动德国代表团关于设立一年一度妇女节的动议——这承接了美国社会主义妇女自 1909 年起举办的妇女日；来自 17 国的约一百名代表通过了它。决议没有指定日期——那留给各国自己决定。

timeline.en: Carried the call through the Secretariat and Die Gleichheit into the movement's papers; on 19 March about a million people took part in meetings and demonstrations in Germany, Austria, Denmark and Switzerland for the vote and for women's labour rights.
timeline.zh: 她通过书记处和《平等报》把这一号召送进各国运动的报刊；3 月 19 日，德国、奥地利、丹麦和瑞士约有一百万人参加集会与示威，要求选举权和女工权利。

timeline.en: Broke with her party's wartime truce and convened an international socialist women's conference at Bern on 26–28 March — about thirty delegates from eight countries, meeting against their parties' wishes — which issued an appeal against the war; for calling it she was arrested and held four months.
timeline.zh: 她与本党的战时「城堡和平」决裂，3 月 26–28 日在伯尔尼召集国际社会主义妇女会议——来自八国的约三十名代表不顾各自政党的意愿前来——会议发出反战呼吁；她因召集此会被捕，关押四个月。

timeline.en: Was among the founders of the Spartacus group in 1916; helping found the USPD in 1917 cost her Die Gleichheit after twenty-five years, and in 1919 she joined the newly formed KPD.
timeline.zh: 1916 年，她是斯巴达克派的创建者之一；1917 年参与创建独立社会民主党，使她失去了主编二十五年的《平等报》；1919 年她加入新成立的德国共产党。

timeline.en: Entered the Reichstag as a KPD deputy, holding the seat until 1933, and spoke there for the first time on 2 July demanding solidarity with Soviet Russia.
timeline.zh: 她以德共议员身份进入国会，议席保持到 1933 年；7 月 2 日首次在国会发言，要求声援苏俄。

timeline.en: Chaired the second International Conference of Communist Women in Moscow in June, which adopted 8 March as the communist movement's date for International Women's Day in memory of the women's demonstration in Petrograd in 1917 — other countries and movements fell in with it only gradually; she sat on the Communist International's executive until 1933.
timeline.zh: 6 月，她主持在莫斯科举行的第二届国际共产主义妇女大会，会议采用 3 月 8 日作为共产主义运动纪念国际妇女节的日期，以纪念 1917 年彼得格勒的妇女示威——其他国家和政治组织只是逐渐跟进；她此后任共产国际执行委员会委员直至 1933 年。

timeline.en: Became president of the International Red Aid, the relief organisation for political prisoners and their dependants — an office distinct from heading its German section — and held it until 1933.
timeline.zh: 她出任国际赤色救济会主席，为政治犯及其家属提供援助——这一职务有别于德国分会的负责人——一直担任到 1933 年。

timeline.en: On 30 August, as the Reichstag's oldest member, she opened the newly elected chamber in which the Nazi party held the largest bloc. Gravely ill and helped to the rostrum, she spoke for some forty minutes: the order of the hour, she said, was a united front of all working people to throw back fascism — and she closed, communist to the last, with the hope of one day opening a congress of soviets of a Soviet Germany. Her KPD colleagues applauded; the united front she asked for never formed.
timeline.zh: 8 月 30 日，她以国会最年长议员的身份主持新一届国会开幕——这届国会中纳粹党是第一大党团。她病重，被人扶上讲台，讲了约四十分钟：当务之急，她说，是结成全体劳动者的统一战线，把法西斯主义打回去——她以共产党人的身份收尾，期望有朝一日主持苏维埃德国的第一次代表大会开幕。德共议员为她鼓掌；她所呼吁的统一战线终究没有形成。

timeline.en: Left Germany after the KPD was banned and died on 20 June at Archangelskoje near Moscow, aged 75, still the movement's longest-serving voice for working women.
timeline.zh: 德共被取缔后她离开德国，6 月 20 日在莫斯科附近的阿尔汉格尔斯科耶去世，享年七十五岁——她始终是这场运动中为女工发声最久的人。

coda.en: The United Nations began observing International Women's Day in 1975; its 1977 resolution invited every state to choose a day for women's rights and international peace according to its own traditions — most chose the 8 March her Copenhagen motion had left open.
coda.zh: 联合国于 1975 年开始纪念国际妇女节；1977 年的决议邀请各国依自身传统选择一天纪念妇女权利与国际和平——多数国家选了她在哥本哈根的动议未曾指定的 3 月 8 日。

story.en:
Barred from party work by the Anti-Socialist Laws, she wrote her way through eight years of exile in Zurich and Paris.

She edited Die Gleichheit from 1892 to 1917, taking it to 124,000 copies; in 1907 she was elected to head the socialist women's international, and in August 1910 she helped carry the German delegation's Copenhagen motion for an annual Women's Day. It named no date. On 19 March 1911 about a million people took part in the first one.

In 1915 she convened the Bern women's conference against the war and went to prison for it.

At 75, opening the Reichstag on 30 August 1932, she called for a united front of all working people against fascism — and, communist to the last, for a Soviet Germany. Her party applauded; the front never formed.
story.zh:
《反社会党人法》断了她在国内的党务之路，她便在苏黎世和巴黎的八年流亡里靠写作立足。

1892 至 1917 年她主编《平等报》，发行量做到十二万四千份；1907 年当选社会主义妇女国际组织负责人；1910 年 8 月，她在哥本哈根参与推动德国代表团设立一年一度妇女节的动议——动议没有指定日期。1911 年 3 月 19 日，约一百万人参加了第一次妇女节的集会与示威。

1915 年，她召集伯尔尼反战妇女会议，并为此入狱。

七十五岁，1932 年 8 月 30 日主持国会开幕，她呼吁全体劳动者结成反法西斯的统一战线——也以共产党人的身份，呼唤一个苏维埃德国。她的党为她鼓掌；统一战线终究没有形成。

era.zh: 维多利亚至爱德华时代 · 英国

intro.en: Refused by the Middlesex Hospital and by the medical schools of London, Edinburgh and St Andrews, she qualified in 1865 through the Society of Apothecaries, whose regulations — her father's lawyers argued, and the Society's own counsel agreed — applied to every candidate who had met them. She spent the next forty years building what the profession would not give her: a dispensary that became a women's hospital, a school where women could train and which she led as dean, a seat on the first London School Board and, at seventy-two, the mayoralty of Aldeburgh.
intro.zh: 米德尔塞克斯医院和伦敦、爱丁堡、圣安德鲁斯的医学院都拒收她；1865 年，她借药剂师公会的执照取得行医资格——她父亲请来的律师主张，公会章程对一切合乎规定的考生一体适用，公会自己的法律顾问也认可了这一点。此后四十年，她自己造出了行业不肯给她的东西：一间诊所，后来成为女子医院；一所女性可以入读、由她出任院长的医学院；首届伦敦学务委员会的一个席位；以及七十二岁时的奥尔德堡市长之职。

timeline.en: She went to Elizabeth Blackwell's London lectures on medicine as a profession for women and, at twenty-three, decided to become a doctor.
timeline.zh: 她去听伊丽莎白·布莱克韦尔在伦敦讲「医学作为女性的职业」，二十三岁的她就此决定当医生。

timeline.en: She took a place as a nursing student on the surgical ward of the Middlesex Hospital and sat in on lectures and dissections for six months, then lost that place after the male students petitioned against her, and was refused entry to the hospital's medical school; the schools of London, Edinburgh and St Andrews refused her too.
timeline.zh: 她在米德尔塞克斯医院外科病房谋得一个护理学生的位置，旁听讲课和解剖课达六个月；男学生联名上书反对后，她失去了这个位置，申请入读该院医学院也遭拒绝；伦敦、爱丁堡和圣安德鲁斯的医学院同样拒收了她。

timeline.en: She registered as a student with the Society of Apothecaries, which examined and licensed apothecaries under its charter and the Act of 1815, read privately with licensed teachers and served an apothecary's apprenticeship. When the Society moved to keep her from its examination, she pressed her case with legal opinions her father had paid for, and its own counsel advised that a candidate who had met the regulations could not be refused.
timeline.zh: 她向药剂师公会注册为学生——该会依据特许状和 1815 年法案主持药剂师考试并颁发执照；随后她跟持照教师私下研读，并完成药剂师学徒期。公会想把她挡在考场外时，她拿着父亲出钱请来的法律意见据理力争；公会自己的法律顾问认为，符合章程的考生不能被拒。

timeline.en: She wrote to the President of the Royal College of Physicians on 5 April asking to sit the College's examinations instead. The College refused; her letter and its reply survive in the College's archive.
timeline.zh: 4 月 5 日，她致信皇家内科医师学会会长，请求改考该学会的执照考试。学会拒绝了；这封信和回信至今保存在学会档案中。

timeline.en: She passed the Licentiate of the Society of Apothecaries on 28 September — three of seven candidates passed, she with the highest marks — and her name followed onto the British Medical Register, the first woman to have qualified in Britain openly as a woman. The Society then amended its regulations to require attendance at a recognised medical school, and the route she had taken was closed for the time being.
timeline.zh: 9 月 28 日，她通过药剂师公会执照考试：七名考生中有三人及格，她分数最高；她的名字随后列入英国医师登记册，成为首位公开以女性身份在英国本土取得资格的女医生。公会随即修改章程，要求考生须在认可的医学院就读，她走过的这条路暂时关上了。

timeline.en: She opened St Mary's Dispensary for Women and Children at 69 Seymour Place in June, where women could be treated by a woman doctor; in its first year 3,000 new patients made 9,300 visits. That year she and Emily Davies also carried the first mass women's suffrage petition, 1,499 signatures, to Westminster.
timeline.zh: 六月，她在西摩街 69 号开办圣玛丽妇幼诊所，让女病人可以找女医生看病；第一年接诊新病人 3,000 名，就诊 9,300 人次。同年，她和埃米莉·戴维斯把第一份大规模妇女选举权请愿书——1,499 个签名——送到了威斯敏斯特。

timeline.en: She taught herself French, entered the Faculty of Medicine of Paris, passed its five examinations and defended a thesis on migraine on 15 June, the first woman to take the Paris medical doctorate. The British Medical Register would not recognise the degree; it was her 1865 licence that authorised her practice.
timeline.zh: 她自学法语，进入巴黎大学医学院，通过五门考试，6 月 15 日以一篇关于偏头痛的论文答辩通过，成为首位取得巴黎医学博士学位的女性。英国医师登记册不承认这个学位；她在英国行医，凭的仍是 1865 年的执照。

timeline.en: She was elected to the first London School Board on 29 November, topping the poll in Marylebone with what The Spectator called that week 'far the highest poll on the list'. She and Emily Davies were the only women on the board, and she served until 1873.
timeline.zh: 11 月 29 日，她当选首届伦敦学务委员会委员，在梅里波恩选区名列第一，用当周《旁观者》的话说，「得票远高于名单上任何人」。全会只有她和埃米莉·戴维斯两名女性，她任职至 1873 年。

timeline.en: She turned the dispensary into the New Hospital for Women, staffed by women, giving women doctors both patients and professional posts; in 1890 she moved it into purpose-built premises on Euston Road.
timeline.zh: 她把诊所扩建为新妇女医院，全院由女性出诊，既为病人看病，也为女医生提供专业岗位；1890 年，她把医院迁入尤斯顿路上专门建造的院舍。

timeline.en: She was admitted to the British Medical Association as its first woman member, and kept her place when the association voted in 1878 to admit no more women; she remained its only woman member until the bar was lifted in 1892, nineteen years after she joined.
timeline.zh: 她获准加入英国医学会，成为该会首位女性会员；1878 年医学会表决不再接纳女性，她没有退出，从 1873 年入会算起的十九年里，她一直是会中唯一的女性，直到 1892 年禁令解除。

timeline.en: She was among the founders of the London School of Medicine for Women, set up by Sophia Jex-Blake with others, and lectured there from 1875 to 1897. That year she also answered Henry Maudsley in the Fortnightly Review, arguing from the record that educating women thoroughly had been tried often and had proved of service, not injurious to their health.
timeline.zh: 她是索菲娅·杰克斯－布莱克与他人共同创办的伦敦女子医学院的创办人之一，并于 1875 至 1897 年在该校授课。同年她在《双周评论》上回应亨利·莫兹利，以既有事实立论：认真教育女性已被反复试过，结果证明有益，而非有害于她们的健康。

timeline.en: She served as dean of the London School of Medicine for Women for nineteen years and oversaw its expansion. In 1878 she had told women thinking of medicine that their work would be scrutinised more closely than men's, and recommended good temper as a working instrument.
timeline.zh: 她担任伦敦女子医学院院长十九年，主持了学院的扩张。早在 1878 年，她就告诉有意学医的女性：她们的专业工作会比男性受到更严苛的审视；她还把好脾气推荐为一件实用的工具。

timeline.en: She was elected mayor of Aldeburgh on 9 November, the first woman mayor in England. At seventy-two she had also joined the Women's Social and Political Union, speaking for it and joining a deputation to the House of Commons; she withdrew her support in 1911 as its militancy escalated.
timeline.zh: 11 月 9 日，她当选奥尔德堡市长，是英格兰第一位女市长。同在七十二岁那年，她加入了妇女社会政治同盟，为其演讲，并参加了前往下议院的请愿团；1911 年，随着该组织行动日趋激烈，她撤回了支持。

timeline.en: She died at Aldeburgh on 17 December, aged 81.
timeline.zh: 12 月 17 日，她在奥尔德堡去世，享年 81 岁。

coda.en: In 1918 the New Hospital for Women — the hospital, not the medical school — was renamed the Elizabeth Garrett Anderson Hospital; its work continues in the Elizabeth Garrett Anderson Wing at University College Hospital.
coda.zh: 1918 年，新妇女医院——是医院，不是医学院——更名为伊丽莎白·加勒特·安德森医院；今天它的工作延续在大学学院医院的伊丽莎白·加勒特·安德森院区。

story.en:
Refused by the medical schools, she found an examining body whose regulations she could meet, and in 1865 the Society of Apothecaries licensed her with the highest marks of the day. The Society then tightened its rules, so that for a time no woman could follow.

She built what the profession would not give: a dispensary that saw 3,000 new patients in its first year and grew into a women's hospital, a Paris MD, the top of a London poll, and a school for women doctors that she led for nineteen years. Her licence let one woman in; her institutions kept the door open for others.

“Women can less easily afford to be second-rate.”
story.zh:
医学院都拒收她，她便去找一家规定自己能够满足的考试机构：1865 年，药剂师公会以当日最高分给了她执照。公会随即收紧章程，一时之间再没有女性能循此路进来。

她自己造出了行业不肯给的东西：一间第一年接诊 3,000 名新病人、后来长成女子医院的诊所；一个巴黎的医学博士学位；伦敦一场选举的头名；还有一所她执掌十九年的女子医学院。执照放进来的是她一个人，她建起的机构把门为后来者撑开。

「女性更承担不起做二流。」

intro.en: She helped build modern obstetrics and gynaecology in China through the ward, the laboratory and the classroom. She was the first Chinese woman kept on as a physician in Peking Union Medical College Hospital's obstetrics and gynaecology department, from 1940 the first Chinese woman to head a department there, and in 1955 one of the first academicians of the Chinese Academy of Sciences — state and institutional accounts describe her as the only woman among the 233 selected that year. She researched tumours, organised cervical-cancer screening with colleagues, trained the doctors who came after her, and in 1982 chief-edited Gynaecological Tumours. She never married.
intro.zh: 她在病房、实验室和课堂里参与奠定了中国现代妇产科学的基础。她是北京协和医院妇产科第一位毕业留院的中国女医师，1940 年起是协和第一位中国籍女科主任；1955 年入选中国科学院首届学部委员，官方与机构的记述都说她是那年当选的 233 人中唯一的女性。她研究肿瘤，与同事一起组织宫颈癌普查，培养了一代又一代医生，1982 年主编出版《妇科肿瘤》。她终身未婚。

timeline.en: Born on 23 December on Gulangyu, the island off Xiamen. Her mother died of cervical cancer when she was five. She finished the Xiamen women's normal school in 1919 and stayed on to teach.
timeline.zh: 12 月 23 日生于厦门鼓浪屿。五岁时母亲因宫颈癌去世。1919 年从厦门女子师范学校毕业，并留校任教。

timeline.en: Travelled to Shanghai in July to sit the entrance examination of Peking Union Medical College. By the account the hospital and the gazetteers still tell, she broke off her own English paper to carry a candidate who had fainted in the heat out of the hall; an invigilator wrote down what she had done, and the college weighed that report with her marks. She entered that autumn, one of a handful of women in her class.
timeline.zh: 7 月赴上海参加北京协和医学院入学考试。据医院与地方志至今沿用的说法，英文考试时有女生中暑晕倒，她中断自己的答卷把人抬出考场；监考者记下此事，校方将这份报告与她的成绩一并考量。当年秋天入学，是班上为数不多的女生之一。

timeline.en: Graduated in June with the M.D. and the Wenhai Scholarship, awarded to one graduate of each class. On 1 July she joined the hospital's obstetrics and gynaecology department, the first Chinese woman graduate kept on there as a physician; by later accounts her appointment was written so that marriage, pregnancy or childbirth would dissolve it. She went on to serve as chief resident.
timeline.zh: 6 月毕业，获医学博士学位与「文海奖学金」——该奖每届只授一人。7 月 1 日进协和医院妇产科，成为该科第一位毕业留院的中国女医师；据后来的记述，聘书写明任职期间结婚、怀孕、生育即自动解约。其后她担任总住院医师。

timeline.en: Trained at medical schools in London and Manchester and made a study visit to Vienna, then did research at the University of Chicago's medical school in 1939–40. She turned down a Chicago gynaecologist's recommendation that she stay on, and went home in 1940.
timeline.zh: 先后到英国伦敦、曼彻斯特的医学院进修，并赴维也纳考察；1939—40 年在美国芝加哥大学医学院做研究。当地一位妇科专家推荐她留校，她谢绝了，1940 年回国。

timeline.en: Took charge of obstetrics and gynaecology at Peking Union Medical College Hospital, the first Chinese woman to head a department there. Over the following decades she studied the intrauterine respiration of the fetus, trophoblastic tumours and female genital tuberculosis, and with colleagues including Song Hongzhao built gynaecological oncology at Union.
timeline.zh: 出任北京协和医院妇产科主任，是协和第一位中国籍女科主任。此后几十年里，她研究胎儿宫内呼吸、滋养细胞肿瘤和女性生殖系统结核，并与宋鸿钊等同事一起建立起协和的妇科肿瘤学。

timeline.en: After Japanese forces closed the hospital in January, she opened a gynaecology clinic at No. 10 Dongtangzi Hutong in Beijing, lowered her registration fee and treated poor women free or for next to nothing. She kept it open until 1948; 8,887 case records survive from those six years — a record of consultations, not of births. Some accounts date the clinic from 1941.
timeline.zh: 1 月协和医院被日军关闭后，她在北平东堂子胡同 10 号开设妇科诊所，主动降低挂号费，穷苦病人免费诊治。诊所开到 1948 年，六年间留下 8887 份病历——那是门诊记录，不是接生数。也有记载把开办年份写作 1941 年。

timeline.en: Headed obstetrics and gynaecology at Peking University Medical School as well, and returned to Union's wards when the hospital reopened in 1948, teaching at the bedside and training specialists.
timeline.zh: 同时兼任北大医学院妇产科主任；1948 年协和医院复院后回到病房，继续临床教学，培养专科医生。

timeline.en: Selected in the first cohort of academicians of the Chinese Academy of Sciences; state and institutional accounts describe her as the only woman among the 233 chosen that year. She sat as a deputy to the first through fifth National People's Congresses and became a vice-president of the Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences in 1959.
timeline.zh: 当选中国科学院首届学部委员；官方与机构的记述都称她是那年当选的 233 人中唯一的女性。她是第一至第五届全国人大代表，1959 年出任中国医学科学院副院长。

timeline.en: Helped carry cervical smear screening out of the clinic and into the city, working within the programme run by the Beijing health bureau and the Cancer Hospital of the Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences, which went house by house through the residents' committees and screened 51,609 women of eligible age in 1960. In 1962 she and her colleagues summed up three years of it: until the cause of the disease was understood, mass screening was the only way to control it, and a nationwide cancer-detection network was imperative.
timeline.zh: 参与把子宫颈涂片检查从门诊推向全市：这项普查由北京市卫生局和中国医学科学院肿瘤医院组织，经居民委员会挨门挨户做，1960 年查了 51609 名适龄妇女。1962 年她与同仁总结三年工作：在弄清病因之前，大量普查是控制这种肿瘤的唯一办法，建立全国范围的抗癌网势在必行。

timeline.en: Took on a woman who had lost four pregnancies, the last three infants yellowing and dying within days, and organised an attempt no one at the hospital had made before. With obstetric and paediatric colleagues — Wang Wenbin performing the exchange — she had the newborn's blood exchanged three times over three days, and stayed with him for seven. The child was named Xiehe, after the hospital; the Museum of Chinese Scientists records him as a pioneering case of haemolytic disease of the newborn saved in China. Over the next year the team did twelve exchange transfusions on seven infants.
timeline.zh: 她接下一位连失四胎的产妇——最后三个孩子出生后发黄夭折——组织了一次院内此前没有做过的尝试。她与妇产科、儿科同事协作，由王文彬操作，三天内为新生儿换血三次，她守了七天七夜。孩子取名「协和」；中国科学家博物馆把他记为中国先行救回的新生儿溶血症病例。此后一年多，团队为 7 名患儿做了 12 次换血。

timeline.en: At sixty-three she went with a rural medical team to Hunan, saw more than 1,300 women in three months and trained village health workers and midwives. She edited the plain-language handbooks the countryside could actually use, among them Family Health Adviser and Rural Maternal and Child Health: Questions and Answers.
timeline.zh: 六十三岁那年随医疗队下湖南农村，三个月里诊治一千三百多名妇女，并培训农村卫生员和接生员。她还主编了乡下真能用得上的通俗读本，如《家庭卫生顾问》《农村妇幼卫生问答》。

timeline.en: Served on the World Health Organization's Advisory Committee on Medical Research.
timeline.zh: 任世界卫生组织医学研究顾问委员会顾问。

timeline.en: Saw Gynaecological Tumours through to print as its chief editor, gathering the department's collective clinical experience, and did it from a hospital bed after a stroke abroad in 1978 and a cerebral thrombosis in 1980; the People's Medical Publishing House brought it out in September.
timeline.zh: 以主编身份把《妇科肿瘤》送到印厂——这部书汇集了科室多年的集体临床经验。1978 年出访西欧时中风，1980 年又因脑血栓住院，她是在病床上完成这项工作的；9 月由人民卫生出版社出版。

timeline.en: Died at Peking Union Medical College Hospital on 22 April, aged eighty-one. She had never married and had no children; official accounts credit her with more than fifty thousand deliveries, a long-repeated estimate rather than a count. Her will left her savings of about 30,000 yuan to the hospital nursery, gave her body for dissection, and asked that her ashes be scattered over the sea off Gulangyu.
timeline.zh: 4 月 22 日在北京协和医院去世，享年八十一岁。她终身未婚，没有子女；官方记述说她接生了五万多个婴儿，这是长期沿用的估数，而非确切统计。遗嘱把约三万元积蓄捐给医院托儿所，遗体供医学解剖，骨灰撒在鼓浪屿附近的海面。

coda.en: Staff later wrote down what she said in her last hours, still on the ward in her mind: "Another plump baby — three delivered in one night. How good."
coda.zh: 守在身边的人后来记下了她临终时的话——那时她心里仍在产房：「又是一个胖娃娃，一晚上接生了 3 个，真好！」

story.en:
Her mother died of cervical cancer when she was five. She entered Union in 1921, graduated in 1929 with the prize given to one graduate a class, and stayed on the ward as the department's first Chinese woman physician.

She ran the department from 1940 and built its oncology with her colleagues; kept a hutong clinic through the occupation, leaving 8,887 case files; helped organise smear screening across Beijing and co-wrote its 1962 summary; and that same year organised the rescue of a newborn with haemolytic disease and stayed seven days beside him.

She called herself, by later account, a doctor on duty for a lifetime.
story.zh:
她五岁时，母亲死于宫颈癌。1921 年考进协和，1929 年毕业，拿了每届只授一人的奖学金，留在病房，成为妇产科第一位中国女医师。

1940 年起她主持妇产科，与同事一起建起妇科肿瘤学；沦陷期间在胡同里开诊所，留下 8887 份病历；参与组织全北京的子宫颈涂片普查，1962 年与同仁写下总结；同年组织救治一名溶血症新生儿，守了七天七夜。

后人记下她的自称：一辈子的值班医生。
